commits.author: Josh Mandel
commits.subject: FHIR-55077: Fix RiskAssessment method example ValueSet link
commits.summary: Completed the Applied FHIR-55077 RiskAssessment terminology update by fixing the method example CodeSystem's stale ValueSet canonical.

triage.reviewer_summary: Jira-backed missed application: FHIR-55077 required the RiskAssessment method and outcome terminology artifacts to become experimental Example artifacts, and this commit fixes the remaining method CodeSystem metadata that still pointed at the old non-Example ValueSet canonical.
triage.category_rationale: FHIR-55077 was Applied/Persuasive and concretely resolved to mark the RiskAssessment method and outcome ValueSets and CodeSystems experimental and add Example to each id, url, name, and title. The method CodeSystem had been renamed as an Example artifact, and the active method ValueSet and RiskAssessment bindings already use http://hl7.org/fhir/ValueSet/risk-assessment-method-example, but CodeSystem.valueSet still referenced http://hl7.org/fhir/ValueSet/risk-assessment-method. Because CodeSystem.valueSet is published terminology/conformance metadata for the active CodeSystem, the unchanged source would leave the renamed CodeSystem linked to an obsolete non-Example ValueSet. Updating that canonical is the narrow change required to complete the Jira-directed rename, not optional consistency cleanup or generated collateral.
triage.fhir_spec_impact: The changed file is an authoritative RiskAssessment CodeSystem XML source, not a hard-avoid generated or diagram file. Its valueSet canonical is part of the published terminology/conformance artifact, so leaving the old URL would make the current Example CodeSystem metadata inconsistent with the renamed active ValueSet and bindings.
triage.recommended_reviewer_action: Keep this as a Jira-backed fix completing FHIR-55077's terminology rename; no separate WG path is needed for this narrow canonical alignment.

jira_evidence.explanation: The resolution required the RiskAssessment method and outcome ValueSets and CodeSystems to be experimental Example artifacts, including Example in their ids and urls. That directly requires the method CodeSystem.valueSet metadata to reference the renamed Example method ValueSet canonical rather than the previous non-Example canonical.

caveats: This assessment is limited to the single changed CodeSystem source file; the related method ValueSet and RiskAssessment bindings already use the Example canonical.

The initial linked edit fixed Procedure narrative text but left the same contraction in the Procedure.status comment and the matching Procedure Event mapping exception text.
triage.category_rationale: FHIR-55327 was Applied/Persuasive for FHIR-core Procedure and specifically required spelling the abbreviated word "doesn't" as "does not". The current Procedure source still missed that application in source/procedure/structuredefinition-Procedure.xml, where the authoritative Procedure.status comment retained "authoring system doesn't know", and in source/procedure/procedure-event-mapping-exceptions.xml, where the resource-side exception text for the same Procedure.status comment retained the same wording. The StructureDefinition comment feeds rendered Procedure element guidance and packaged conformance text, and the mapping-exception file is active source used to keep Procedure's Event-pattern mapping exceptions aligned with the resource text. Changing both occurrences is required to complete the exact spelling correction that the Jira approved, rather than an adjacent cleanup or a new editorial policy.
triage.fhir_spec_impact: The Procedure StructureDefinition XML is authoritative conformance source, so the stale comment affects current rendered element guidance and distributed StructureDefinition content. The Event mapping exception file is a Procedure-specific active mapping source; updating its resource text keeps the mapping exception aligned with the corrected Procedure.status comment and avoids preserving the same approved-against contraction in current mapping material.
triage.recommended_reviewer_action: Keep the commit as a Jira-backed editorial correction for FHIR-55327. Review the StructureDefinition hunk as the primary source fix and the event-mapping exception hunk as the necessary synchronized Procedure.status mapping text.

jira_evidence.explanation: The issue is Applied/Persuasive for FHIR-core Procedure, identifies the abbreviated word "doesn't" on the Procedure page, and resolves to spell it out as "does not". That directly requires updating remaining active Procedure source text that still contains the same contraction.

commits.author: Josh Mandel
commits.subject: FHIR-55973: Require distinct repeated Questionnaire answers
commits.summary: Updated active Questionnaire and QuestionnaireResponse source so repeated question answers must be distinct.

triage.reviewer_summary: Jira-backed missed application: FHIR-55973 explicitly resolved that repeated Questionnaire answers must be distinct and that QuestionnaireResponse should prohibit duplicate answers for the same question. The commit updates only the active Questionnaire and QuestionnaireResponse StructureDefinition sources needed to reflect that decision.
triage.category_rationale: FHIR-55973 was Applied/Persuasive and its resolution specifically required three concrete source/spec changes: add a QuestionnaireResponse.item invariant saying answer.value.isDistinct() with human text prohibiting the same answer more than once for the same question; update Questionnaire.item.repeats definition/comment wording from multiple answers to multiple distinct answers; and move the group/question representation note to the start of the repeats comment. Before this commit, the current Questionnaire source still used the older non-distinct repeats wording, and QuestionnaireResponse.item lacked the duplicate-answer invariant and condition reference on answer. These StructureDefinition XML files are authoritative inputs for rendered element definitions, generated conformance resources, and validation constraints. The edit is the exact source application required to complete the Jira resolution, not generated collateral, optional consistency cleanup, or a separate editorial improvement.
triage.fhir_spec_impact: The Questionnaire edit changes reader-visible definition/comment text for Questionnaire.item.repeats. The QuestionnaireResponse edit adds an error-level invariant and condition reference, affecting generated conformance artifacts and validation behavior for repeated answer values.
triage.recommended_reviewer_action: Keep this as the Jira-backed fix for FHIR-55973; no alternate attribution, subset filtering, or new WG path is needed for these source changes.

jira_evidence.explanation: The Applied/Persuasive resolution explicitly required distinct-answer wording in Questionnaire.item.repeats and a QuestionnaireResponse.item invariant prohibiting the same answer more than once for the same question. The commit implements those requirements in the active StructureDefinition sources.

caveats: The invariant expression is implemented as answer.value.isDistinct().allTrue(), which preserves the Jira-requested distinct-value rule while fitting the surrounding FHIRPath constraint style.

The missed application is that the active core CodeSystem definition and the reader-visible defined-properties table still referenced includeLastVersionPresent, an earlier parameter name that no longer matches the CRMI resolution. Those files publish the current concept-property definition and explanatory table, so the stale text directs implementers to the wrong CRMI parameter. Replacing the two stale references with includeNoLongerPresent is the narrow update required to complete the linked decisions, not generated collateral or optional consistency cleanup.
triage.fhir_spec_impact: source/codesystem/codesystem-concept-properties.xml is authoritative CodeSystem source for the concept-property definition, and source/codesystem/codesystem-notes.xml supplies the rendered defined concept-properties table. triage.recommended_reviewer_action: Keep the change as a Jira-backed correction, and cite FHIR-55634 alongside FHIR-56201 so the final includeNoLongerPresent parameter decision is visible in the review history.

jira_evidence.explanation: This Applied/Persuasive with Modification CRMI issue finalized the ValueSet/$expand input parameter as includeNoLongerPresent and says returned concepts SHOULD have the lastVersionPresent concept property. That resolution directly determines the correct parameter name for the core cross-reference.

This Applied/Persuasive with Modification core issue required adding lastVersionPresent as a string concept property and adding it to the defined concept-properties table. It explains why the property and table text belong in core, but its own resolution text used the intermediate includeLastVersionPresent parameter name.

caveats: The correction is limited to active CodeSystem and narrative source; no generated, SVG, or avoided files are touched.
The shown issue key is only partial attribution because FHIR-55634 is the decision that finalized includeNoLongerPresent.

jira_evidence.explanation: The issue requested and approved adding ImagingStudy.series.instance.numberOfFrames to list the number of frames in a multiframe instance, with unsignedInt cardinality 0..1 and DICOM mapping to Number Of Frames (0028,0008). Updating these surfaces is required to complete the approved application because leaving them unchanged would make validation and reader-facing artifact text contradict the PHWG decision.
triage.fhir_spec_impact: The StructureDefinition constraint changes current conformance and validation behavior for Immunization.statusReason. The invariant test bundles affect QA coverage for that rule, and the SearchParameter, binding, and ValueSet description edits align active rendered/distributed artifact metadata with the approved entered-in-error semantics.

commits.summary: Added Consent-specific rationale strings for all previously Unknown Event mapping exception reasons in the active Consent source file.

triage.reviewer_summary: Jira-backed missed application. FHIR-50873 accepted adding rationale for Consent deviations from the Event pattern, and this commit replaces the remaining Unknown rationale values in the active Consent mapping-exceptions source.
triage.category_rationale: FHIR-50873 is the responsible resolution: it reported the current build message that source/consent/consent-event-mapping-exceptions.xml had Consent/Event pattern differences with an Unknown reason, and the Applied/Persuasive resolution was to add rationale for the deviation. The missed application was that the Consent mapping-exceptions file still contained 34 reason="Unknown" attributes for divergent and unmapped Event pattern surfaces. Those attributes are active pattern-mapping metadata used by the current build/QA process to distinguish accepted Consent-specific divergences from unexplained gaps. Replacing each Unknown value with a non-empty Consent-specific rationale is required to complete the accepted correction; the change is limited to the exact file and rationale attributes named by the Jira/build condition, not generated collateral or optional adjacent cleanup.
triage.fhir_spec_impact: The edit does not change Consent element definitions, cardinalities, bindings, or mappings. Its current impact is on the active Event-pattern mapping exception metadata used for build/QA and reviewer-visible explanation of why Consent intentionally differs from the shared Event pattern.
triage.recommended_reviewer_action: Keep as a Jira-backed fix, with ordinary CBCC review of the precise rationale wording if desired.

jira_evidence.explanation: The issue is an Applied/Persuasive FHIR-core Consent technical correction. Its description quotes the build message that source/consent/consent-event-mapping-exceptions.xml had Event-pattern differences with an Unknown reason, and its resolution says to add rationale for the deviation; replacing those Unknown reason attributes directly implements that decision.

A prior DiagnosticReport recommendation change touched the same Consent mapping-exceptions file only as background. It did not resolve the missing Consent/Event rationale request and is not the attribution for this change.

caveats: This is a QA/pattern-metadata correction rather than a change to normative Consent conformance semantics.
FHIR-50873 requires adding rationales but does not prescribe the exact wording, so reviewers may refine the rationale text without changing the triage conclusion.

commits.author: Josh Mandel
commits.subject: FHIR-48924 + FHIR-47323: Correct Device maintenance extension names
commits.summary: Corrected the Device ballot note so removed Device maintenance elements point to the actual Extension Pack ids.

triage.reviewer_summary: Jira-backed missed application: the Device introduction still pointed readers to obsolete or non-existent maintenance extension ids. The edit aligns the reader-visible Device guidance with the approved operation-specific Device maintenance extensions.
triage.category_rationale: FHIR-32565 required Device.mode, Device.cycle, Device.duration, Device.gateway, and Device.endpoint to move out of core Device into extensions; FHIR-48924 approved the Device maintenance extension proposal and called for implementer notes about the new core extensions; FHIR-47323 created the concrete maintenance extensions for mode, cycle, and duration with ids device-operation-mode, device-operation-cycle, and device-operation-duration. The missed application is in source/device/device-introduction.xml, where the Device introduction said the removed mode, cycle, and duration elements were replaced by device-mode, device-cycle, and device-duration even though those are not the approved ids. That file is rendered as Device resource narrative, so the stale names misdirect implementers looking for the replacement extensions for removed core elements. Replacing only those three ids is required to complete the approved removal-and-extension application; it is not generated collateral, optional consistency cleanup, or a separate editorial preference, and the gateway and endpoint names were already correct.
triage.fhir_spec_impact: The changed file is Device resource introduction narrative, so the stale text affects current reader-visible guidance. The change does not alter Device conformance structure, but it corrects published guidance from non-existent maintenance extension ids to the actual extension-pack ids.
triage.recommended_reviewer_action: Keep this as a Jira-backed Device guidance fix. Treat the attribution as shared: FHIR-48924 provides the core approval and implementer-note requirement, while FHIR-47323 provides the exact extension ids used in the correction.

jira_evidence.explanation: FMG approved creating Device maintenance extensions tied to the elements removed from core, and the Jira comment says implementer notes are needed because core extensions are being added for mode, duration, and cycle.

The FHIR-extensions issue resolved that the maintenance extensions would be created, recorded operation-specific ids device-operation-mode, device-operation-cycle, and device-operation-duration, and was applied in the extension-pack implementation.

This approved moving Device.mode, Device.cycle, Device.duration, Device.gateway, and Device.endpoint out of core Device into extensions, establishing why the Device introduction must refer readers to replacement extensions.

caveats: The shown issue is a valid core approval reference, but the exact operation-specific ids come from the linked FHIR-extensions decision and implementation.
Only source/device/device-introduction.xml is changed; no generated, derived, or hard-avoid file is part of this commit.

The active ImagingSelection StructureDefinition still had copied structure-set wording in the waveFormChannel requirement, and this one-line correction completes the approved conformance text.
triage.category_rationale: FHIR-52900 was resolved as Persuasive/Applied with a linked draft update that removed ImagingSelection.instance.subset and added explicit subset elements, including ImagingSelection.instance.waveFormChannel for channels selected from a waveform SOP Class. The current authoritative StructureDefinition incompletely applied that resolution because waveFormChannel.requirements still said the element was allowed only when instance.sopClass corresponded to a waveform structure set SOP Class. That requirements value is part of the current element definition used for rendered detailed descriptions and generated conformance artifacts, so the stale phrase made the conformance-facing rule contradict the approved waveform-channel model. The proposed edit is required and sufficient to complete the Jira application because it changes only that stale requirement to waveform SOP Class and does not include generated diagrams, ignored fixtures, or unrelated cleanup.
triage.fhir_spec_impact: source/imagingselection/structuredefinition-ImagingSelection.xml is the active authoritative StructureDefinition source for ImagingSelection. The edited requirement is rendered in element details and carried in conformance output, so the stale structure-set phrase affected current reader-visible and conformance-facing requirements for ImagingSelection.instance.waveFormChannel.
triage.recommended_reviewer_action: Keep this as a Jira-backed conformance correction under FHIR-52900. Treat any similar wording in generated SVGs or old negative fixture text as separate artifact-maintenance cleanup rather than part of this source correction.

jira_evidence.explanation: FHIR-52900 resolved to apply the linked ImagingSelection subset draft, replacing instance.subset with explicit mutually exclusive subset elements. The draft specifically ties waveFormChannel to waveform SOP Class selections, making the existing structure-set requirement wording an incomplete application of the approved change.
FHIR-49907 covered Imaging QA issues and related example/exception updates in the same resource area, but it does not specifically require the waveFormChannel requirement wording fixed here.
FHIR-50859 concerns ImagingStudy and ImagingSelection bodySite/laterality changes. It does not decide the ImagingSelection subset split or the waveform-channel requirement wording.

caveats: The concrete wording comes from the draft update incorporated by the FHIR-52900 resolution; the Jira itself delegates the detailed source changes to that linked material.
This judgment applies to the StructureDefinition correction only; generated diagrams or ignored fixture residue should be regenerated or cleaned separately if editors want them synchronized.

commits.author: Josh Mandel
commits.subject: FHIR-53270: Correct Requirements category change metadata
commits.summary: Corrected the active R5-to-R6 change metadata so it records the applied statement-level Requirements category element.

triage.reviewer_summary: This is a Jira-backed missed application: the R5-to-R6 change metadata still identified a new top-level Requirements.category even though the approved and current element is Requirements.statement.category. Keeping the source/fhir.ini correction aligns the release-change surface with the applied Requirements StructureDefinition.
triage.category_rationale: FHIR-53270 was Applied/Persuasive with Modification for R6 and specifically approved allowing requirement statements to carry 0..* category values, using Coding rather than the originally suggested CodeableConcept. The current Requirements StructureDefinition implements that decision as Requirements.statement.category, but the R5-to-R6 change metadata still recorded Requirements.category as the added element. That stale metadata is a missed application because it names a non-current top-level path instead of the Jira-approved statement-level element in the release-change surface. Replacing it with Requirements.statement.category is required to complete the approved change metadata and is not merely optional cleanup, generated collateral, or later terminology work.
triage.fhir_spec_impact: source/fhir.ini is the editor-owned release-change metadata used for current R5-to-R6 change information. Before this edit, that current metadata could report a new Requirements.category element that is absent from the authoritative conformance source, instead of the actual Requirements.statement.category Coding element.
triage.recommended_reviewer_action: Keep this as a Jira-backed fix to the R5-to-R6 change metadata. Treat later binding and code-system work under FHIR-54023/UP-783 separately, and handle any remaining SVG reference only through regeneration or diagram-specific cleanup.

jira_evidence.explanation: The resolved request was to allow requirement statements to have 0..* category values, with the approved modification that the datatype be Coding. That directly supports the statement-level Requirements.statement.category path and contradicts release-change metadata that still names a top-level Requirements.category.

This later resolved issue concerns creating a THO code system and preferred binding for Requirements.statement.category. It confirms the current element path in later discussion, but it does not independently justify this metadata correction or any terminology edits here.
The UTG proposal is related to the future requirement category code system and remains a separate terminology path. It is not needed to justify correcting the R5-to-R6 element path metadata.

triage.tooling_recommendation: Add a consistency check that flags R5-to-R6 change entries whose element paths are absent from the current StructureDefinitions.
caveats: This classification covers only the source/fhir.ini metadata correction; it does not apply the later preferred binding or THO code system work.

The remaining Requirements.category reference in source/requirements/requirements.svg appears to be diagram collateral and should be regenerated or handled separately rather than hand-edited as part of this source fix.

commits.author: Josh Mandel
commits.subject: FHIR-51523: Correct supportingInfo subCategory application
commits.summary: Corrected the applied Claim and ExplanationOfBenefit supportingInfo.subCategory definitions so they match the approved 0..* CodeableConcept change.

triage.reviewer_summary: This is a Jira-backed missed application: FHIR-51523 explicitly approved Claim and ExplanationOfBenefit supportingInfo.subCategory as 0..* CodeableConcept. The commit corrects the authoritative resource StructureDefinitions to match that decision, including an ExplanationOfBenefit id/path copy error.
triage.category_rationale: FHIR-51523 resolved to add supportingInfo.subCategory to Claim and EOB as 0..* CodeableConcept with the definition 'Finer-grained categorization of the information'. The current application had added the element but left Claim.supportingInfo.subCategory and ExplanationOfBenefit.supportingInfo.subCategory with max 1, and the ExplanationOfBenefit element was still identified and pathed as Claim.supportingInfo.subCategory. These StructureDefinition XML files are the authoritative resource sources for rendered element tables, generated conformance artifacts, and validation behavior, so the single-valued cardinality and copied Claim identity directly conflict with the approved resource structure. Changing both max values to * and correcting the ExplanationOfBenefit id/path is required to complete the approved application rather than being adjacent cleanup.
triage.fhir_spec_impact: The changed files are authoritative Claim and ExplanationOfBenefit StructureDefinition XML. Without this correction, the current specification would publish and validate supportingInfo.subCategory as single-valued instead of repeating, and the ExplanationOfBenefit conformance element would carry the wrong Claim element identity/path.
triage.recommended_reviewer_action: Keep this as a Jira-backed fix for FHIR-51523; no new Jira, rollup issue, or WG path is needed for these StructureDefinition corrections.

jira_evidence.explanation: The resolution specifically says to add supportingInfo.subCategory to Claim and EOB as 0..* CodeableConcept with the finer-grained categorization definition. That directly requires repeating cardinality on both resources and the ExplanationOfBenefit element to use the ExplanationOfBenefit id/path.

This related Financial Management decision says ClaimResponse supportingInfo should mirror Claim and EOB, including R6 supportingInfo structure changes such as subCategory. It supports the broader consistency context but is not needed to justify the Claim and ExplanationOfBenefit corrections in this commit.

caveats: The changed files are editor-owned authoritative conformance source, and no hard-avoid generated or SVG files are included.

triage.category_rationale: FHIR-51522 resolved to add ClaimResponse.supportingInfo mirroring Claim and EOB, explicitly including approved R6 changes to that structure such as subCategory; FHIR-51523 supplies the concrete subCategory element as 0..* CodeableConcept. The existing ClaimResponse StructureDefinition had only an incorrectly identified ClaimResponseResponse.supportingInfo element and omitted ClaimResponse.supportingInfo.subCategory, so the prior application was incomplete. Because source/claimresponse/structuredefinition-ClaimResponse.xml is the editor-owned conformance source for the active ClaimResponse resource, those mistakes affect the generated StructureDefinition and rendered resource definition. Fixing the element id and adding the subCategory child are necessary to complete the approved mirroring, rather than optional cleanup or generated collateral.
triage.fhir_spec_impact: The changed file is the authoritative ClaimResponse StructureDefinition XML. triage.recommended_reviewer_action: Keep the commit as a Jira-backed fix for FHIR-51522, with FHIR-51523 as supporting context for the exact subCategory shape being mirrored.

jira_evidence.explanation: The resolution says to add ClaimResponse.supportingInfo mirroring Claim and EOB with R6 supportingInfo changes such as subCategory. That directly requires a correctly identified ClaimResponse.supportingInfo backbone and inclusion of the approved subCategory child.

The resolution approved supportingInfo.subCategory on Claim and EOB as 0..* CodeableConcept. Since FHIR-51522 explicitly incorporates those R6 supportingInfo changes into ClaimResponse, this supplies the concrete child definition to mirror.

commits.author: Josh Mandel

This commit updates the active Appointment StructureDefinition binding, the authoritative conformance source for that element.
triage.category_rationale: FHIR-51886 was an Applied/Persuasive Patient Administration correction for R6 whose resolution specifically required updating the broken Appointment.class value set link from https://terminology.hl7.org/ValueSet/EncounterClass to https://terminology.hl7.org/ValueSet/encounter-class. The current Appointment StructureDefinition binding still used the uppercase EncounterClass URL, so the approved repair was missed on the active source surface. That binding feeds generated conformance artifacts and rendered binding links, so the stale URL affects current specification correctness rather than only source cleanliness. Changing the valueSet to the lowercase encounter-class canonical is the narrow required edit to complete the approved Jira application.
triage.fhir_spec_impact: source/appointment/structuredefinition-Appointment.xml is an active resource StructureDefinition source. The inspected commit only changes the authoritative StructureDefinition XML, not a checked-in SVG or other generated-looking collateral.

commits.author: Josh Mandel
commits.subject: FHIR-50011: Correct terminology relatedArtifact constraint sources
commits.summary: Corrected constraint source metadata for the FHIR-50011 relatedArtifact invariants on CodeSystem, ConceptMap, and NamingSystem.

triage.reviewer_summary: Jira-backed missed application: FHIR-50011 required resource-specific relatedArtifact restrictions on CodeSystem, ConceptMap, NamingSystem, and ValueSet, but the copied constraints on the three non-ValueSet resources still claimed ValueSet as their source. Keep the metadata correction because these StructureDefinition XML files are authoritative current conformance inputs.
triage.category_rationale: FHIR-50011 was Applied/Persuasive for R6 and specifically required relatedArtifact invariants on CodeSystem, ConceptMap, NamingSystem, and ValueSet that prohibit depends-on and composed-of, with successor/predecessor target restrictions handled as non-executable guidance after review. The current source had the required prohibition constraints on CodeSystem, ConceptMap, and NamingSystem, but each active constraint still carried ElementDefinition.constraint.source = http://hl7.org/fhir/StructureDefinition/ValueSet, showing that the ValueSet template was copied without completing the resource-specific metadata application. These StructureDefinition XML files are authoritative resource definitions used to generate current conformance and rendered constraint metadata, so the stale canonical misstates the origin of active resource-local constraints. Changing csd-8, cmd-14, and nsd-4 to point to CodeSystem, ConceptMap, and NamingSystem is required to complete the approved resource-specific application rather than being adjacent cleanup or a separate editorial preference.
triage.fhir_spec_impact: The edit does not change the FHIRPath expressions enforced by validation, but it corrects current generated StructureDefinition constraint metadata and rendered constraint information for active terminology resources. This is conformance metadata in editor-owned source, not generated collateral or repository-only hygiene.
triage.recommended_reviewer_action: Keep as the FHIR-50011-backed metadata fix. Do not expand this review to add executable successor/predecessor resolve() constraints, because the Jira follow-up records that those were deliberately omitted after review discussion.

jira_evidence.explanation: The resolution required relatedArtifact invariants on CodeSystem, ConceptMap, NamingSystem, and ValueSet, including type != depends-on and type != composed-of for each resource. Because those are resource-specific constraints declared in the corresponding StructureDefinitions, the copied ValueSet source canonical on the non-ValueSet constraints is an incomplete application of the approved change.
This broader RelatedArtifact guidance issue is cited by FHIR-50011 as the basis for applying resource-specific restrictions, but the concrete terminology-resource requirement comes from FHIR-50011.

triage.tooling_recommendation: Consider adding a StructureDefinition consistency check that flags ElementDefinition.constraint.source canonicals copied from another resource when the constraint key is resource-local.
caveats: The fix is limited to constraint source metadata; it intentionally preserves the existing depends-on/composed-of expressions and the recorded decision not to add executable resolve() constraints for successor/predecessor targets.

commits.author: Josh Mandel

triage.fhir_spec_impact: The changed file is an active DeviceMetric narrative source file, so the impact is reader-visible formatting in the rendered Boundaries and Relationships section. It does not change conformance resources, terminology, examples, validation behavior, or QA semantics.
triage.recommended_reviewer_action: Keep as a Jira-backed formatting correction for the active DeviceMetric narrative page. No additional Jira or WG path is needed unless the work group wants to revisit the broader resource-name styling convention.

jira_evidence.explanation: The issue requested review of DeviceMetric pages and source/devicemetric content for correct font use of element names and, if applicable, resource names; the accepted resolution was to update formatting at editor discretion following common FHIR practice. That directly supports correcting the inconsistent plain DeviceMetric resource-name reference in the DeviceMetric Boundaries and Relationships narrative.

Later DeviceMetric Boundaries and Relationships work added the DeviceAlert bullet containing the unstyled DeviceMetric reference. It explains how the localized regression appeared, but FHIR-51404 is the formatting decision that justifies the correction.

commits.author: Josh Mandel

commits.summary: Aligned Composition.custodian prose with the already-applied Organization, Patient, and Group target profiles.

This commit updates the StructureDefinition short and definition so the rendered element text matches the already-applied target profiles.

Because this StructureDefinition is the authoritative source for the Composition element table and generated conformance resource, the stale prose would remain reader-visible and inconsistent with the allowed Reference targets. Updating these two prose fields is required to complete the Jira application because the old wording directly contradicts the Patient target added for the same resolved change, rather than being optional consistency cleanup.
triage.fhir_spec_impact: The changed file is authoritative Composition StructureDefinition source. triage.recommended_reviewer_action: Keep this as a Jira-backed fix to the StructureDefinition prose. If the work group later wants Person instead of, or in addition to, Patient and Group, handle that as a separate decision because the final resolution here names Organization, Patient, and Group.

jira_evidence.explanation: The issue requested changing Composition.custodian away from Reference(Organization) for patient-authored notes, and the final resolution says to update it to Organization|Patient|Group. That directly requires both the target profiles and the element prose to include Patient alongside Organization and Group.

triage.tooling_recommendation: Consider checking Reference target-set changes against element short/definition prose so stale descriptive text is flagged when target profiles are updated.

Earlier request or planning wording may have mentioned Person, but the final Jira resolution and applied target-profile change use Organization, Patient, and Group.

commits.author: Josh Mandel
commits.subject: FHIR-38735: Align dateTime offset comment
commits.summary: Corrected the active dateTime primitive comment so it no longer says UTC offsets are allowed on date-only or partial-date values.

triage.reviewer_summary: Jira-backed missed application. FHIR-38735 resolved that a timezone offset is permitted only when a full time is specified, but the active dateTime primitive comment still said UTC offsets were allowed for dates and partial dates.
triage.category_rationale: FHIR-38735 was a Published/Persuasive R5 technical correction for the dateTime regex, and the final Jira comment explicitly states that timezone is only permitted if time, meaning full time, is specified, with the earlier regex attachment to be applied. The prior source application corrected the regex direction but left source/datatypes/primitives.xml saying "UTC offset is allowed for dates and partial dates", which directly contradicted the resolved rule and later current regex behavior. That primitive spreadsheet row is an authoritative datatype source for rendered primitive datatype documentation, so the stale comment remained a current reader-visible specification contradiction. This edit is required to complete the approved correction because it changes the contradictory active comment to the Jira-resolved rule without adding generated collateral, optional cleanup, or a new policy change.
triage.fhir_spec_impact: source/datatypes/primitives.xml is an authoritative primitive datatype source used for current datatype rendering. The change affects the rendered dateTime datatype comment; it does not alter validation behavior because the regex has already been brought into line with allowing date-only values while not allowing offsets on date-only or partial-date values.
triage.recommended_reviewer_action: Keep this as a Jira-backed fix attributed to FHIR-38735. Treat FHIR-52878 as later supporting context for the current regex behavior, not as a replacement attribution or a reason to make additional regex changes here.

jira_evidence.explanation: The Published/Persuasive R5 technical correction addressed the dateTime regex rejecting date-only values, and its final comment says timezone is only permitted when full time is specified. That directly requires removing the active primitive comment that said UTC offsets are allowed for dates and partial dates.

The later Applied/Persuasive R6 clarification moved timezone syntax inside the time branch of the dateTime regex. It reinforces that offsets should not be described as allowed on date-only or partial-date values, but the missed comment update is already justified by FHIR-38735.

caveats: The commit changes only the active dateTime primitive comment; no generated, derived, or hard-avoid files are included.
Any future decision about whether the regex should enforce every dateTime rule, including offset presence whenever a time is present, would be separate from this comment correction.

commits.author: Josh Mandel
commits.subject: FHIR-51699: Align DeviceAlert value set metadata

The commit narrowly completes that metadata portion for authoritative ValueSet XML sources.

The missed application is that the DeviceAlert ValueSets were made active, but most source/devicealert/valueset-devicealert-*.xml files still had publisher "FHIR Project team" and contact URL "http://hl7.org/fhir" instead of the WG metadata required for those ValueSets. triage.fhir_spec_impact: The changed files are current core DeviceAlert ValueSet source files. Their publisher and contact elements are part of generated conformance resources and rendered terminology pages, so leaving the generic FHIR Project team metadata would publish incorrect owner/contact metadata for these ValueSets.
triage.recommended_reviewer_action: Keep as a Jira-backed fix. Treat FHIR-51699 as the direct basis for the ValueSet publisher/contact update, with FHIR-55949 supporting the current "HL7 International / Devices" wording; leave extension-pack URL alignment and later THO movement to their separate tickets.

jira_evidence.explanation: The Applied/Persuasive with Modification resolution required DeviceAlert code systems and value sets to have active status, correct URL treatment, WG publisher/contact metadata, and an activationState spelling correction. The later application comments narrowed the core CodeSystem URL change but did not remove the ValueSet publisher/contact requirement.

This Applied technical correction establishes that the current work group name is "Devices" rather than the older "Health Care Devices" wording used in FHIR-51699, supporting the exact publisher value used here.
This unresolved FHIR-extensions ticket records related extension-pack URL alignment created from FHIR-51699. It helps bound the scope but is not the basis for changing the core ValueSet metadata.

This later resolved proposal would move several DeviceAlert terminology artifacts to THO, but it does not supersede the need for correct current core metadata while these ValueSet sources remain in core.

caveats: FHIR-51699's original text used "Health Care Devices"; FHIR-55949 supports using the current "Devices" WG label in the publisher string.
The commit intentionally does not alter core CodeSystem canonical URL shapes, consistent with the Jira application comment and committers discussion.

commits.author: Josh Mandel
commits.subject: FHIR-53884: Mark security vocabulary guidance informative

This Published/Persuasive issue moved Bundle entry SHALL requirements into invariants while leaving other explanatory language. This older Published/Persuasive with Modification issue removed the former requirement that every history entry contain a transaction because versions can be created outside REST interactions. This later Published issue said to include PATCH in the history resource rule, but that conflicts with the current PATCH prohibition for history request methods. It should be handled separately rather than as the basis for this update.

triage.reviewer_summary: Jira-backed missed application: FHIR-33004 required the Measure evaluate reportType value set to contain only the evaluation report types individual, subject-list, and summary. The current compose inherited the later-added other MeasureReport.type code, so this authoritative ValueSet source should be tightened as proposed.
triage.category_rationale: FHIR-33004 was Applied/Persuasive and its later application comment made the concrete requirement explicit: create MeasureReportEvaluationType for evaluate-measure with individual, subject-list, and summary, and bind reportType to that value set. The current source surface missed that requirement by implementing the value set as all measure-report-type codes except data-exchange; after the shared code system gained other, the evaluation value set no longer represents the Jira-required three-code set. This matters because the file is the authoritative terminology source bound from the active Measure evaluate reportType parameters, so its expansion affects the operation conformance surface. Enumerating individual, subject-list, and summary is necessary to complete the Jira application rather than optional cleanup, because leaving the transitive include/exclude compose permits a report type the Jira-requested evaluation set and operation prose do not include.
triage.fhir_spec_impact: source/measure/valueset-measure-report-evaluation-type.xml is an active authoritative ValueSet used by the Measure $evaluate-measure and $evaluate OperationDefinition reportType bindings. As written before this change, its expansion includes other even though the operation documentation lists only individual, subject-list, and summary, so the current conformance output can allow a code outside the intended evaluation report types.
triage.recommended_reviewer_action: Keep this source fix as the completion of the FHIR-33004 application. Revisit only through a new CQI decision if evaluate reportType should intentionally accept implementation-defined other reports.

jira_evidence.explanation: The Applied/Persuasive resolution required correcting Measure $evaluate-measure reportType by creating a value set that does not contain data collection/data-exchange and binding reportType to it. A later Jira comment gives the exact source target: MeasureReportEvaluationType with individual, subject-list, and summary.

This Applied issue described FHIR-33004 as not applied and requested a dedicated evaluate-measure reportType value set excluding data-exchange, then marked the same implementation commit as applying it. It supports the evaluation-only intent but is not needed as the primary attribution.

This issue introduced the newer Measure $evaluate operation and carried forward the same reportType binding, explaining why the corrected ValueSet now affects both active evaluate operation definitions.

The later addition of the other MeasureReport.type code explains why the original all-codes-except-data-exchange compose became too broad. It changed the shared code system, not the evaluate operation's three-code intent.

triage.tooling_recommendation: Consider a terminology consistency check for operation-specific ValueSets that are modeled as broad shared-code-system includes with exclusions when the operation text or Jira decision defines a closed explicit subset.
caveats: The commit changes only the editor-owned ValueSet source and does not include generated or layout-only collateral.

commits.author: Josh Mandel
commits.subject: FHIR-50487 + FHIR-51066: Clarify evaluatedResource report scopes
commits.summary: Updated the active MeasureReport.evaluatedResource definition so it no longer implies either all server resources or individual reports only; it now distinguishes individual-report subject-specific resources from data-exchange data-of-interest.

triage.reviewer_summary: This is a Jira-backed missed application with mixed attribution: FHIR-34033 explains the bounded evaluatedResource intent, but the direct need to allow data-exchange reports comes from later CQI data-exchange decisions. The edit updates the active MeasureReport StructureDefinition so its evaluatedResource text no longer contradicts current collect-data and submit-data use.
triage.category_rationale: FHIR-50487 required R6 submit-data alignment with DEQM and specifically described quality-reporting Bundles containing MeasureReports and data of interest in MeasureReport.evaluatedResources; FHIR-51066 required collect-data responses to return data-exchange MeasureReports with data-of-interest resources referenced from evaluatedResource; and FHIR-39174 confirmed data-exchange as the expected submit-data report type. The missed application is that the current MeasureReport.evaluatedResource StructureDefinition still said evaluated resources were only allowed or reported for individual reports, which conflicts with those approved data-exchange surfaces. Because this element text is authoritative StructureDefinition source used for rendered definitions and generated conformance resources, leaving the old wording would make approved data-exchange examples and operations appear inconsistent with the resource definition. Updating the committee note, short, definition, and comment is required to complete the later Jira applications while preserving FHIR-34033's bounded-resource concern; it is not generated collateral or optional cleanup.
triage.fhir_spec_impact: The changed file is the active, authoritative MeasureReport StructureDefinition source. Its evaluatedResource short, definition, comment, and committee note affect rendered resource definitions and generated conformance content, and the stale individual-only wording conflicted with current collect-data/submit-data operation text and examples that use data-exchange MeasureReports with evaluatedResource references.
triage.recommended_reviewer_action: Keep the source change as a Jira-backed fix, but review it under FHIR-50487 and FHIR-51066 rather than FHIR-34033 alone; FHIR-34033 is supporting context for bounded evaluatedResource wording.

jira_evidence.explanation: The applied CQI resolution aligned Measure $submit-data with DEQM and required quality-reporting guidance where Bundles contain MeasureReports and data of interest in MeasureReport.evaluatedResources. That approved data-exchange use cannot coexist with a resource definition saying evaluatedResource is only allowed for individual reports.

The applied CQI resolution aligned Measure $collect-data with DEQM; the current applied operation text returns Bundles whose MeasureReports have type data-exchange and whose data-of-interest resources are referenced from the corresponding MeasureReport.evaluatedResource elements. This directly requires the MeasureReport element definition to allow data-exchange reports.

The applied CQI resolution confirmed that submitted MeasureReports are expected to use the data-exchange report type, supporting the later data-exchange context that made the old individual-only evaluatedResource wording obsolete.

The published CQI resolution required MeasureReport.evaluatedResource wording that avoided implying all resources considered by a server and kept reports bounded. Its original application introduced the individual-report-only wording now being reconciled with later approved data-exchange use.

caveats: The commit changes only editor-owned StructureDefinition source; it does not include generated, derived, or hard-avoid files.
FHIR-34033 alone would not justify broadening evaluatedResource to data-exchange reports; the clean justification depends on the later applied data-exchange Jira decisions.

triage.recommended_reviewer_action: Keep the commit as the remaining Jira-backed Medication Module guidance for FHIR-34293.

jira_evidence.explanation: The resolution states that detectedIssue will be removed from both MedicationRequest and MedicationDispense and that guidance will be added in the Medication Module on how to access associated detected issues. This directly requires the edited module guidance.

commits.author: Josh Mandel
commits.subject: FHIR-32960: Align vaccine administration guidance
commits.summary: Aligned active MedicationAdministration and Immunization narrative guidance so vaccines are primarily represented with Immunization while MedicationAdministration remains allowed for vaccination workflow reasons when an equivalent Immunization instance is also created and exposed.

triage.reviewer_summary: Jira-backed missed application: FHIR-32960 specifically resolved the MedicationAdministration vaccine boundary wording by directing vaccine administration to Immunization while preserving MedicationAdministration only for workflow or similar reasons when an equivalent Immunization instance is also created and exposed. This commit completes that clarification in the active MedicationAdministration and Immunization narrative pages.
triage.category_rationale: FHIR-32960's Published/Persuasive resolution required concrete source wording: Scope and Usage should refer vaccine treatment to the Immunization resource, and Boundaries should say vaccine administration is intended for Immunization while allowing MedicationAdministration for vaccination workflow or other reasons only if systems also create and expose an equivalent Immunization instance. The earlier application left current narrative text out of alignment: MedicationAdministration still retained the obsolete resource/Profile wording and spaced resource name, and the paired Immunization Boundaries paragraph still said MedicationAdministration was for non-vaccine medications and used the older, less explicit equivalent-Immunization wording. These introduction files are active resource narrative pages, so the missed text affects reader-visible guidance about the Immunization/MedicationAdministration boundary. The proposed edits are required to finish the approved clarification rather than optional cleanup because they remove wording that directly contradicts or incompletely states the accepted boundary rule.
triage.fhir_spec_impact: The changed files are active resource introduction narrative pages. They affect rendered guidance about whether vaccine administration should be represented with Immunization, when MedicationAdministration is allowed for vaccination workflows, and whether an equivalent Immunization instance must be created and exposed; they do not change conformance structures.
triage.recommended_reviewer_action: Keep as a Jira-backed fix. Review the wording as completion of the approved FHIR-32960 clarification across the paired active resource-boundary pages.

jira_evidence.explanation: The issue asked to resolve conflicting MedicationAdministration vaccine wording, and the accepted resolution gave concrete Scope and Boundaries text: vaccine administration is intended to be handled using Immunization, MedicationAdministration is for medication administration, and if MedicationAdministration is used to capture vaccinations for workflow or other reasons, systems should also create and expose an equivalent Immunization instance.

This older issue explains the historical wording that treated MedicationAdministration as covering medications and vaccines and pointed to Immunization for vaccines. It is background only; FHIR-32960 is the later clarifying decision.

This older issue explains the historical equivalent-Immunization language. It supports why the stale exception wording existed but is superseded in practice by FHIR-32960's more specific clarification.

caveats: The Immunization page was not the artifact named in the Jira metadata, but it contained the same active boundary guidance and still contradicted the accepted FHIR-32960 rule.
No generated, SVG, or editor-avoided files are part of this commit.

commits.author: Josh Mandel

triage.reviewer_summary: Jira-backed missed application. FHIR-34195 specifically required a missing-value meaning for the optional MedicationRequest.reported boolean, and the current MedicationRequest StructureDefinition still carried that approved meaning only as a general comment on the renamed element.
triage.category_rationale: FHIR-34195 was Published/Persuasive and resolved that MedicationRequest.reported should state that, when missing, the request is assumed to be the original record and not reported; because the request was for meaningIfMissing on a non-mandatory boolean, the concrete source requirement is ElementDefinition.meaningWhenMissing. The earlier application placed the approved sentence in ElementDefinition.comment, and later current-source work renamed the same element to MedicationRequest.isRecordOfRequest while preserving that comment, leaving the structured missing-value field absent. The edited file is the authoritative MedicationRequest StructureDefinition input, so the omission affects generated conformance metadata and rendered element semantics for the current resource. Moving the exact approved sentence from comment to meaningWhenMissing is required to complete the Jira application, rather than being optional cleanup, because a comment does not encode the missing-value semantics the Jira requested.
triage.fhir_spec_impact: The changed file is authoritative StructureDefinition source for MedicationRequest. The update changes current conformance output by populating ElementDefinition.meaningWhenMissing for MedicationRequest.isRecordOfRequest and removes the same text from the less precise comment field; it is not generated-file synchronization or repository-hygiene-only cleanup.
triage.recommended_reviewer_action: Keep this as a Jira-backed missed application for FHIR-34195 on the current renamed element. Treat FHIR-49863 only as context explaining the current element name, not as the responsible decision for the missing-value semantics.

jira_evidence.explanation: The issue asked that the non-mandatory MedicationRequest.reported boolean have meaningIfMissing, and the approved resolution supplied the exact missing-value meaning: if missing, assume this is the original record and not reported. That directly requires the approved sentence to be encoded as ElementDefinition.meaningWhenMissing on the current corresponding element.

This later Pharmacy change renamed MedicationRequest.reported to MedicationRequest.isRecordOfRequest and changed related element semantics. It supports applying the FHIR-34195 missing-value text to the renamed current element, but it is not the source of the missing-value requirement.

caveats: The commit changes only the editor-owned MedicationRequest StructureDefinition hunk; it does not include hard-avoid SVG, generated modelinfo, or derived collateral files.

commits.author: Josh Mandel

triage.category_rationale: FHIR-15755 was Published as Persuasive with Modification and specifically required adding Composition.section.focus, a composition-section-subject extension for cases needing it, guidance that resources in a focused section match the section focus as their logical subject, and a labor-and-delivery mother/child example showing a different section focus from the Composition subject. The current source already contains the Composition.section.focus element and associated guidance, but the checked-in mixed Composition example created for this application omitted the focus element on the mother section, so the example did not demonstrate the concrete behavior the resolution called for. Adding focus Reference(Patient/infant-mom) to the mother section is the direct missing source application needed for the example to satisfy the Jira decision; the adjacent title typo correction clarifies the same intended mother section and is incidental to the required fix.
triage.fhir_spec_impact: The changed file is an active Composition example source listed for the Composition examples. Without the focus element, the current example set includes a mother/child mixed Composition that does not exercise Composition.section.focus or demonstrate the logical-subject rule required by FHIR-15755; with it, the example shows the section focus on the mother while the Composition subject remains the infant.
triage.recommended_reviewer_action: Keep this as a Jira-backed source fix. Review the focus addition as the missed application of FHIR-15755; the spelling correction can stay because it clarifies the same mother section being fixed.

jira_evidence.explanation: The resolution specifically required Composition.section.focus, a composition-section-subject extension, logical-subject guidance for focused sections, and a labor-and-delivery mother/child example showing subject used with a different section focus. That directly requires the active mixed example to contain an actual focus for the mother section.

This earlier Composition.section issue prompted the later subject/focus discussion, but its own resolution only says to add the requested section content and does not independently justify this example edit.

Later Composition wording involving Composition.section.focus is background only; the available evidence does not indicate that it changed the FHIR-15755 section-focus semantics or the attribution for this example fix.
A later unresolved family-history section-focus question is not a final source-edit decision and is not needed to justify this mother/child example fix.

caveats: The whole commit is confined to source/composition/composition-example-mixed.xml; it does not include generated, derived, SVG, or other hard-avoid files.
The title spelling correction is not the core Jira requirement, but it is a harmless clarification of the same mother section where the Jira-required focus is added.

commits.author: Josh Mandel

commits.summary: Completed the R6 Request pattern application of the new higher-level 'ended' status by fixing the remaining RequestStatus hierarchy metadata and Request.status spreadsheet text.

The commit updates editor-owned Request pattern source rather than generated or diagram collateral.
triage.category_rationale: FHIR-48861 was Applied/Persuasive for R6 and specifically resolved to define a new Request status 'ended' with the quoted definition and make it a parent of terminal request states. The prior application added the ended concept and nested terminal codes under it, but the current RequestStatus CodeSystem still lacked hierarchyMeaning='is-a', Request.status still omitted ended from the spreadsheet short list, and the status guidance still described post-activation terminal states without the new ended grouping. Those omissions leave authoritative Request pattern inputs inconsistent with the approved status hierarchy and with the generated/conformance interpretation of the nested concepts. Adding the hierarchy meaning and updating the Request.status spreadsheet text is required to complete the approved change; cleaning the duplicate literal text in the same ended row corrects the same newly added source cell rather than changing unrelated collateral.
triage.fhir_spec_impact: source/request/codesystem-request-status.xml is the RequestStatus CodeSystem source, so hierarchyMeaning controls the formal meaning of the nested ended/completed/revoked concepts in generated conformance output. source/request/request-spreadsheet.xml is the active Request logical pattern spreadsheet, so the short list and comments feed current rendered Request.status documentation and implementer-facing guidance.
triage.recommended_reviewer_action: Keep the commit as the Jira-backed completion of FHIR-48861 for the RequestStatus CodeSystem and Request.status spreadsheet source. Separate WG review would only be needed for a future decision to add distinct stopped/cancelled generic RequestStatus codes rather than continuing to represent non-completed termination with revoked.

jira_evidence.explanation: The resolution explicitly says to define a new Request status 'ended' with the quoted definition and make it a parent of completed, stopped, and cancelled terminal states. In the current generic RequestStatus code system, that decision was partially applied as ended with completed/revoked children, but the CodeSystem hierarchy metadata and Request.status spreadsheet text still did not fully expose the approved parent status.

Workflow meeting minutes record FHIR-48862 in the same decision family, but it is not needed as the responsible decision for these edits; FHIR-48861 directly supplies the status hierarchy requirement.

caveats: FHIR-48861 names stopped and cancelled as terminal examples, while the current generic RequestStatus vocabulary uses revoked for non-completed termination; this commit correctly avoids adding new terminal codes without a separate WG decision.

commits.author: Josh Mandel
commits.subject: FHIR-37567: Split ActivityDefinition PRN reason elements
commits.summary: ActivityDefinition now represents PRN use with separate asNeeded and repeatable asNeededFor elements, and includes the requested PRN usage example.

triage.reviewer_summary: Jira-backed missed application: FHIR-37567 explicitly approved separate ActivityDefinition PRN elements and a PRN usage example, but the current source still had a single asNeeded[x] choice and no ActivityDefinition example. This commit updates the authoritative ActivityDefinition structure and registers the requested ibuprofen-as-needed example.
triage.category_rationale: FHIR-37567's Published/Persuasive CDS resolution required adding ActivityDefinition.asNeeded as a 0..1 Boolean, ActivityDefinition.asNeededFor as a 0..* CodeableConcept, and an example of the suggested PRN usage. The missed application was that the prior source retained ActivityDefinition.asNeeded[x] as a Boolean-or-CodeableConcept choice and omitted the ActivityDefinition example, so the model could not express asNeeded=true together with multiple reasons such as pain or fever. The StructureDefinition is the authoritative conformance source for ActivityDefinition, and the registered example is current example source, so the stale choice and missing example affect generated conformance content, rendered element tables, validation shape, and distributed examples. Splitting the element, carrying forward the binding and invariant, and adding/registering the ibuprofen example are required to complete the Jira application rather than optional consistency cleanup.
triage.fhir_spec_impact: The StructureDefinition change affects current generated ActivityDefinition conformance content, rendered element tables, and validation behavior by replacing the asNeeded[x] choice with separate asNeeded and repeatable asNeededFor elements. The new list entry registers an ActivityDefinition example that demonstrates the requested PRN usage and should be visible or distributed with the current ActivityDefinition examples.
triage.recommended_reviewer_action: Keep this as the ActivityDefinition Jira-backed fix. Do not broaden it into PlanDefinition, DeviceRequest, ServiceRequest, or other PRN consistency changes without separate work group decisions.

jira_evidence.explanation: The Published/Persuasive CDS resolution says to add ActivityDefinition asNeeded and asNeededFor elements as suggested and include the suggested usage example; the issue text specifies asNeeded 0..1 Boolean, asNeededFor 0..* CodeableConcept, and pain-or-fever PRN usage.

This Published Pharmacy issue established the same split asNeeded/asNeededFor pattern for Dosage and clarified that multiple asNeededFor reasons mean any one condition may justify PRN use. It supports the semantics used here but is not the responsible ActivityDefinition decision.
This Published DeviceRequest PRN decision is a similar change family for a different artifact and work group. It does not justify applying broader non-ActivityDefinition changes in this commit.

caveats: The commit changes only ActivityDefinition XML source files and does not include hard-avoid SVG or generated model-definition files.
Broader PRN alignment for PlanDefinition or other request resources should be handled separately if a work group wants that consistency.

triage.reviewer_summary: This is a real current-spec correction: Immunization.statusReason should not point readers to the obsolete reasonCode element when the current resource uses Immunization.reason. The cited Jira supports the performed-reason versus status-reason distinction, but it does not itself require the later current-name update.
triage.category_rationale: FHIR-14377 required adding Immunization.statusReason for not-done reasons while keeping performed-immunization reasons in reasonCode/reasonReference under the then-current Event-style model. The current StructureDefinition now has Immunization.reason as the CodeableReference element for performed reasons, so the statusReason comment's reference to reasonCode is stale and misleading in rendered definitions and conformance metadata. However, the necessary current edit follows from a later model-name/CodeableReference merge rather than from the concrete FHIR-14377 resolution, and no issue-specific resolution was identified that explicitly required updating this statusReason comment to Immunization.reason.
triage.fhir_spec_impact: source/immunization/structuredefinition-Immunization.xml is authoritative StructureDefinition source, so the comment is rendered and distributed in the Immunization conformance definition. The mapping-exceptions update keeps a source companion file consistent with the same wording, but the primary current spec impact is the active StructureDefinition comment.
triage.recommended_reviewer_action: Apply or review this as a real correctness fix under the Jira that authorized the reasonCode/reasonReference to Immunization.reason merge, or under a small cleanup/rollup issue if no better attribution exists. Do not treat FHIR-14377 alone as complete attribution for the current element-name change.

jira_evidence.explanation: The resolution established the separation between Immunization.statusReason for not-done reasons and performed-reason elements, but it specifically spoke in terms of adding statusReason, renaming reason to reasonCode, adding reasonReference, and binding those reason elements. It supports why the comment should distinguish statusReason from performed reasons, but not the later replacement of reasonCode/reasonReference wording with Immunization.reason.

This issue was closed by reference to FHIR-14377 and contains the same Event-pattern rationale for distinct Immunization.reason and Immunization.statusReason concepts. It is context for the distinction, not a separate resolution requiring this exact current wording.

The R6 resolution updated the statusReason short, definition, comment, and invariant for not-done/entered-in-error statuses, but its resolved comment text still used reasonCode. It shows the stale wording survived a recent statusReason edit, but it does not clearly authorize replacing reasonCode with Immunization.reason.

caveats: The active source records Immunization.reasonCode and Immunization.reasonReference as merged into Immunization.reason.concept/reference, but the available evidence ties that to broad version-diff/change-annotation history rather than a clear Immunization-specific Jira resolution.
The StructureDefinition hunk is the reviewer-critical spec fix; the mapping-exceptions hunk appears to be consistency collateral for the same wording.

commits.author: Josh Mandel
commits.subject: FHIR-48547: Remove duplicate package composition guidance
commits.summary: Removed duplicate package-composition guidance introduced by two independent applications of FHIR-48547, leaving one canonical section and one ImplementationGuide link.

triage.reviewer_summary: This is a Jira-backed missed application: FHIR-48547 required package-composition warning guidance and an ImplementationGuide link, but the approved guidance was left duplicated in active documentation source. The commit removes the duplicate copies while preserving one canonical section and a compatibility anchor.
triage.category_rationale: FHIR-48547 was Applied as Not Persuasive with Modification and specifically required adding a Packages page section warning that very large packages can make real-world tools struggle or fail, plus an ImplementationGuide-resource note linking to that guidance. The missed application is that the same approved change was applied twice: source/packages.html contained an early Package composition section and a later FHIR Package Composition section with the same warning, and source/implementationguide/implementationguide-notes.xml contained two paragraphs sending readers to the package guidance. Those files are active reader-facing specification source, so the duplicate sections and competing fragment links affect current rendered package and ImplementationGuide guidance. Removing the extra early section and extra ImplementationGuide paragraph, while retaining one canonical FHIR Package Composition section and preserving the old package-composition anchor, is the narrow edit required to finish the Jira application rather than an adjacent cleanup.
triage.fhir_spec_impact: source/packages.html is active package documentation and source/implementationguide/implementationguide-notes.xml contributes to active ImplementationGuide narrative. Before this change, readers would see the same package-composition warning twice and the ImplementationGuide notes would contain two local link paragraphs; after it, the approved warning and link remain once, with both anchors resolving to the retained section.
triage.recommended_reviewer_action: Keep as a Jira-backed fix. Review it as a narrow duplicate-application cleanup for FHIR-48547, preserving the canonical package-composition guidance and the compatibility fragment anchor.

jira_evidence.explanation: The resolution declined a numeric package size cap but specifically required a Package composition section warning authors about large-package consequences and an ImplementationGuide link to that guidance. The current source had duplicate applications of that exact approved content, so removing the duplicate copies is required to leave the Jira-required guidance once.

This later package-spec issue concerns adjacent NPM package and ImplementationGuide-reference wording. It does not justify the duplicate-removal edit, but it supports preserving the separate adjacent package-spec guidance rather than treating it as part of the duplicate FHIR-48547 material.

caveats: No generated, derived, or hard-avoid files are touched; both changed files are editor-owned active documentation source.
The retained section has both composition and package-composition anchors, so existing links to the earlier fragment continue to resolve.

triage.recommended_reviewer_action: Keep the focused module-page table update as a Jira-backed fix. Attribute the consistency requirement to FHIR-50630, the explicit MolecularDefinition and GenomicStudy table-content requirement to FHIR-51647, and the CG Incubator link targets to FHIR-54345.

jira_evidence.explanation: The applied persuasive resolution accepted a request to make the Diagnostics module diagram and table consistent; the request specifically identified GenomicStudy as present in the diagram but missing from the table.

commits.author: Josh Mandel
commits.subject: FHIR-24629: Correct continuous variable Measure example
commits.summary: Corrected the applied continuous-variable Measure example and completed the requested QM IG examples narrative reference.

FHIR-24629 required adding a continuous-variable Measure example from the Quality Measure IG and adding narrative references to QM IG Measure examples; the applied source left the EXM55 example internally broken and omitted the requested narrative reference.
triage.category_rationale: FHIR-24629's Applied/Persuasive resolution specifically required adding a continuous-variable Measure example to the base Measure resource and adding narratives that reference the QM IG for additional Measure examples, while not moving the continuous-variable profile into core. The current source incompletely applied that requirement: the EXM55 group linkId used a malformed value- attribute, the measure-observation inputPopulationId did not point to the actual measure-population linkId, and the Measure examples header lacked the requested QM IG examples reference. triage.fhir_spec_impact: Both changed files are editor-owned Measure source surfaces. The EXM55 XML is a rendered and distributed Measure example, so the malformed linkId and broken inputPopulationId affect the example's conformance meaning. The examples header contributes rendered Measure examples narrative, so the added QM IG link completes reader-visible guidance requested by the resolution.
triage.recommended_reviewer_action: Keep this as a Jira-backed fix for FHIR-24629. Review the XML fixes and header edit together because they complete the same requested continuous-variable Measure example work.

jira_evidence.explanation: The Applied/Persuasive CQI resolution says to add a continuous-variable Measure example to the base Measure resource and add narratives referencing the QM IG for additional Measure examples. A later comment identifies the QM IG EXM55 example as the source to pare down and says it should demonstrate Initial Population, Measure Population, MeasureObservation, aggregation method, and criteria reference elements, which requires the native R6 linkId and inputPopulationId references in the example to be coherent.

This later Measure ballot cleanup touched adjacent examples prose and deprecated Measure example elements, but it did not require or complete the EXM55 continuous-variable example corrections or the QM IG examples link.
