commits.author: Josh Mandel
commits.subject: FHIR-32859: Describe MedicationRequest status as request lifecycle
commits.summary: Fixed remaining MedicationRequest.status wording so the status element, binding, search parameter, mapping exception mirror, and diagram tooltip describe a request lifecycle rather than a prescription/order lifecycle.

triage.reviewer_summary: This is a Jira-backed missed application: FHIR-32859 required MedicationRequest.status wording to describe the status lifecycle as applying to a request, not just to a prescription/order. The commit completes that correction in active MedicationRequest StructureDefinition, search parameter, and Request-pattern mapping exception XML source.
triage.category_rationale: FHIR-32859 was Published/Persuasive with Modification and specifically resolved that MedicationRequest status states should use "request" instead of "prescription" because MedicationRequest covers plans and proposals as well as orders, with an additional observation-reference fix. The status CodeSystem definitions were already corrected, but current MedicationRequest.status source still described the element as the state of an order, the binding as the state/lifecycle of a prescribing event or prescription, the status search parameter as the status of the prescription, and the Request-pattern mapping exception mirror as the state of the order. These are current source surfaces for rendered/conformance-facing MedicationRequest status text. Changing them to request-centered wording is required to finish the approved status wording application, not a broader optional terminology sweep.
triage.fhir_spec_impact: The StructureDefinition edits affect the generated MedicationRequest element definition, binding description, rendered element table, and conformance resource. The SearchParameter bundle edit affects the published MedicationRequest-status SearchParameter description. The mapping exception edit keeps the current Request-pattern mapping exception text aligned with the corrected status definition. The commit does not include generated-library files or SVG diagram collateral.
triage.recommended_reviewer_action: Keep this as the Jira-backed MedicationRequest.status wording fix for FHIR-32859. Do not broaden it into unrelated prescription/order wording changes without separate Pharmacy WG direction; any diagram tooltip collateral should be regenerated or handled outside this source fix.

jira_evidence.explanation: The issue states that MedicationRequest covers plans and proposals and that status states should not use prescription wording in a way that implies prescription-only scope. The resolution says to change to "request" instead of "prescription" and fix an observation reference, which directly supports correcting remaining MedicationRequest.status descriptions that still say prescription, prescribing event, or order.

caveats: The changed files are XML source files; checked-in SVG diagram collateral is intentionally not part of this commit and should not be hand-edited as part of this triage.
The Request-pattern mapping exception hunk is justified because it mirrors the same MedicationRequest.status definition that FHIR-32859 required to be request-centered.

commits.author: Josh Mandel
commits.subject: FHIR-22824: Clarify continuous-variable score type
commits.summary: Clarified how continuous-variable MeasureReport measureScore[x] choice types are determined after confirming the requested non-Quantity score choices and aggregateMethod promotion were already present.

triage.reviewer_summary: Jira-backed missed application: FHIR-22824 explicitly required documentation that the continuous-variable MeasureReport measureScore[x] type is determined by the result type of the aggregateMethod operation. This commit adds that missing clarification to active quality-reporting narrative and MeasureReport element comments.
triage.category_rationale: FHIR-22824 was Published/Persuasive and required three concrete source/spec outcomes: add dateTime, CodeableConcept, Period, Range, and Duration as possible MeasureReport measureScore value types; promote aggregateMethod to Measure; and document that, for continuous-variable measures, the reported measureScore type is determined by the result type of the aggregate method operation. The value-type additions and aggregateMethod promotion were already applied, but the current quality-reporting guidance and the MeasureReport group and stratum measureScore[x] element comments still omitted the required type-selection rule. Those surfaces are current reader-visible guidance and authoritative StructureDefinition element documentation, so the omission leaves the specification without a rule the Jira resolution expressly called for. The proposed edit is necessary to complete that documentation requirement and does not include generated collateral, optional cleanup, or unrelated files.
triage.fhir_spec_impact: source/clinicalreasoning-quality-reporting.html is rendered quality-reporting guidance, and source/measurereport/structuredefinition-MeasureReport.xml is authoritative conformance source whose comments are exposed with the element definitions. The change clarifies current rendered and conformance documentation for selecting the MeasureReport measureScore[x] value type for continuous-variable reports.
triage.recommended_reviewer_action: Keep as a Jira-backed source fix for FHIR-22824. Review the exact CQI wording if desired, but the files and scope are appropriate for applying the missed documentation requirement.

jira_evidence.explanation: The resolution explicitly says to add the requested MeasureReport measureScore value types, promote aggregateMethod to Measure, and add documentation indicating that the reported type of measureScore for continuous-variable measures is determined by the result type of the aggregate method operation. This commit implements the still-missing documentation portion on active source surfaces.

Related implementation history indicates that aggregateMethod was added as Measure.group.population.aggregateMethod, satisfying the promotion context that FHIR-22824 relied on. It supports why current documentation can refer to aggregateMethod, but the direct documentation requirement comes from FHIR-22824.
Later broader quality-reporting scoring guidance did not include this exact continuous-variable score type rule, so it does not supersede or eliminate the FHIR-22824 documentation requirement.

caveats: The structural MeasureReport score choice changes were already present; this commit should be evaluated as completing the explicit documentation requirement, not as changing the score choice set.
The aggregateMethod promotion appears to have been handled separately, so this commit appropriately limits itself to MeasureReport comments and quality-reporting narrative guidance.

commits.author: Josh Mandel
commits.subject: FHIR-25289: Clarify Timing timeOfDay repetition
commits.summary: Clarified the authoritative Timing.repeat.timeOfDay comment so timeOfDay occurs at the specified time(s) as otherwise constrained by repeat timing, rather than unconditionally implying daily repetition.

triage.reviewer_summary: Jira-backed missed application: FHIR-25289 approved correcting Timing.repeat.dayOfWeek and Timing.repeat.timeOfDay wording after FHIR-12460 so schedules such as twice a day on Mondays and 10:00 AM every other day are expressible. The remaining Timing.repeat.timeOfDay comment still implied unconditional daily repetition, so this focused source edit completes the approved correction.
triage.category_rationale: FHIR-25289 was Published/Persuasive and agreed to change the Timing wording as described, with the request explicitly identifying 10:00 AM every other day as a use case that should be possible after FHIR-12460. The historical application removed the explicit frequency/period exclusion and preserved the FHIR-23710 when-only mutual-exclusion rule, but source/datatypes/timing.xml still said that timeOfDay means the action happens every day, which continued to contradict the approved non-daily timeOfDay use case. Because this spreadsheet is the authoritative Timing datatype source, the stale comment affects generated Timing definition text and implementer-facing conformance documentation. Replacing the unconditional daily inference with wording that defers to the rest of repeat timing is required to finish the approved wording correction, not just adjacent cleanup.
triage.fhir_spec_impact: source/datatypes/timing.xml is the authoritative Timing datatype source, so this comment feeds the current rendered datatype definitions and conformance-facing documentation for Timing.repeat.timeOfDay. The stale wording would tell readers that timeOfDay implies every-day execution even though the current constraints and examples allow frequency/period to constrain the schedule to non-daily intervals.
triage.recommended_reviewer_action: Keep this as a Jira-backed source fix for the Timing datatype. No subset should be dropped and no new WG path is needed for this narrow wording completion.

jira_evidence.explanation: The Published/Persuasive resolution agreed to change the Timing dayOfWeek and timeOfDay wording as described after FHIR-12460, and the request explicitly cited 10:00 AM every other day as a schedule that should be possible. The residual daily-inference sentence in the timeOfDay comment continued to conflict with that approved outcome.

This Published/Persuasive issue approved updating Timing.repeat.timeOfDay so timeOfDay is mutually exclusive only with when. The proposed wording preserves that rule while fixing the remaining daily implication.

This earlier Published/Persuasive with Modification issue loosened Timing constraints so timeOfDay can coexist with frequency and period, explaining why a comment that forces daily repetition independent of frequency/period is stale.

This issue introduced the original timeOfDay comment wording before later Timing constraint changes. It is background for why the old daily-inference sentence became stale, not the current responsible correction.
This unresolved dosage-example issue shows current example interest in timeOfDay with non-daily timing, but it is not needed to justify this wording fix and does not provide the responsible decision.

caveats: The commit changes only source/datatypes/timing.xml and does not include generated, derived, or hard-avoid files.
The fix should remain limited to clarifying the timeOfDay comment; broader Timing examples or dosage-example changes would need their own review path.

commits.author: Josh Mandel

Later no-change discussion reportedly noted related Transport code warnings but did not supersede FHIR-50643 or require changing the approved code literals. It supports keeping this correction limited to the stale terminology metadata.

commits.author: Josh Mandel

commits.summary: Corrected the remaining qualified named-expression examples in the Using Expressions topic from text/cql to text/cql-identifier.

triage.fhir_spec_impact: The changed file is a rendered Clinical Reasoning topic page. triage.recommended_reviewer_action: Keep this as the narrow Jira-backed source fix for the Published correction. No generated files, diagram files, or broader CQL media-type policy changes are part of this commit.

jira_evidence.explanation: The issue requested correction of text/cql uses throughout the Using Expressions topic to text/cql-expression or text/cql-identifier as appropriate. The changed XML and JSON examples are qualified named-expression references, so the resolution requires text/cql-identifier here.

This later issue updated the same Using Expressions topic and made it Normative, but it did not supersede or narrow the earlier media-type correction; the stale qualified-identifier examples remained a separate missed correction.

 source/types.html   | 2 +-
 2 files changed, 2 insertions(+), 2 deletions(-)

triage.reviewer_summary: Jira-backed missed application: this keeps the Defined Concept Properties table and the formal concept-properties CodeSystem synchronized for datatypes, copyable property URLs, and the synonym deprecation metadata. The shown issue is relevant, but the full attribution is mixed because later accepted Jira decisions supply the concrete datatype and replacedBy details.
triage.category_rationale: FHIR-37849 required the CodeSystem Defined Concept Properties table and the http://hl7.org/fhir/concept-properties CodeSystem to be reconciled by retaining the table, adding codes both ways, deprecating the old deprecated property code in the CodeSystem, and keeping deprecated out of the table. Later accepted decisions made the concrete current requirements: FHIR-48428 added explicit dataType metadata to each concept-property concept, FHIR-44627 retired synonym and added deprecation metadata, and FHIR-50433 required replacedByCode and replacedByCoding in both the properties CodeSystem and table with code and Coding datatypes. The current source had missed parts of that application: the rendered table still said date for effectiveDate, deprecationDate, and retirementDate even though the formal concept-property datatype is dateTime; the deprecationDate and retirementDate table copy controls pointed at the status URI; the grouped replacedBy[X] row still said string; and synonym encoded its deprecationDate property as valueCode instead of valueDateTime. These are current specification surfaces: the CodeSystem XML is the distributed conformance resource and the notes XML renders reader-visible CodeSystem narrative. The edit is required to complete the accepted reconciliation because it makes the retained table, property URLs, formal datatype metadata, and value[x] choice usage agree, rather than adding optional collateral or unrelated cleanup.
triage.fhir_spec_impact: source/codesystem/codesystem-concept-properties.xml feeds the published concept-properties CodeSystem, so the synonym concept's deprecationDate value[x] type affects the distributed conformance resource. source/codesystem/codesystem-notes.xml renders the CodeSystem Defined Concept Properties narrative, where readers see the datatypes and can copy the advertised property URIs.
triage.recommended_reviewer_action: Keep the commit as a Jira-backed consistency fix, citing mixed attribution: FHIR-37849 supplies the table/code-system reconciliation requirement, while FHIR-48428, FHIR-44627, and FHIR-50433 explain the current datatype, synonym, and replacedBy details.

jira_evidence.explanation: Published/Persuasive resolution required reconciling section 4.8.12 with the concept-properties CodeSystem, retaining the table, adding codes both ways, deprecating deprecated in the CodeSystem, and keeping deprecated out of the table. That directly requires the retained table and formal CodeSystem to stay aligned.

Applied/Persuasive with Modification resolution added the dataType property to the concept-properties CodeSystem and required values for each property concept, using the concept-property-type value set. This provides the formal datatype surface that the table and value[x] choices must match.

Applied/Persuasive resolution retired the synonym property and added the replacement alternate-code approach. It explains why synonym now carries deprecation metadata, which must use the dateTime-valued deprecationDate property correctly.

Published/Persuasive with Modification resolution required adding replacedByCode of type code and replacedByCoding of type Coding to the properties CodeSystem and table. The pre-commit grouped table row saying string was therefore an incomplete application.

triage.tooling_recommendation: Consider adding a consistency check that compares the Defined Concept Properties table datatypes and copy-button URIs against the concept-properties CodeSystem concepts and dataType metadata, including value[x] choice conformance for properties used inside that CodeSystem.
caveats: FHIR-37849 is a valid umbrella for keeping the retained table and CodeSystem synchronized, but it does not by itself explain every datatype detail introduced by later accepted Jira work.
No generated, derived, layout-only, or hard-avoid files are touched.

Because this StructureDefinition is the authoritative conformance source for the current SubstanceDefinition resource, the stale model affects generated conformance resources, rendered element definitions, validation expectations, and whether current examples can validate. The proposed StructureDefinition changes and the live example updates are required to complete that Jira decision rather than being optional consistency cleanup.

The example changes keep the current SubstanceDefinition example aligned with the approved model by using code-valued active statuses and adding the now-required code.status.
triage.recommended_reviewer_action: Keep this as the Jira-backed source fix for FHIR-31830. Review the SubstanceDefinition conformance changes and live example update together; handle companion medication-definition status issues under their own Jira decisions.

jira_evidence.explanation: The Published/Persuasive with Modification resolution requires SubstanceSpecification/SubstanceDefinition status fields to be datatype code, cardinality 1..1, modifier elements, and constrained to draft/active/retired/unknown using the standard publication-status value set. The issue description specifically calls out SubstanceDefinition.status, code.status, name.status, and name.official.status.

It supports the family-wide pattern but is not the direct attribution for the SubstanceDefinition changes.

This companion BRR issue applied the same required publication-status pattern to other medication-definition resources and Ingredient. It supports consistency across the family but does not replace FHIR-31830 as the direct decision for SubstanceDefinition.

One status occurrence is inside a commented-out example block and has no independent output impact, but the same file also contains live example changes required by the updated conformance model.

triage.reviewer_summary: Jira-backed missed application: FHIR-30092 approved MedicationKnowledge treatmentIntent with an indication-required constraint and an example binding to SNOMED CT therapeutic intents. The current StructureDefinition already had the refactored treatmentIntent element, but still lacked those two approved conformance details.
triage.category_rationale: FHIR-30092 resolved to add MedicationKnowledge administrationGuideline.treatmentIntent as 0..1 CodeableConcept, require indication when treatmentIntent is specified, and make an example binding to children of SNOMED CT 262202000. FHIR-30093 and FHIR-28597 explain the later model inversion, so the current source surface for that requirement is MedicationKnowledge.indicationGuideline.dosingGuideline.treatmentIntent under MedicationKnowledge.indicationGuideline. The prior application added the element on that refactored path but omitted both the indication invariant and the binding. Because this XML is the authoritative StructureDefinition, those omissions affect generated conformance resources, rendered element details, and validation behavior; adding mkn-1, condition references, and the example binding is necessary to finish the approved Pharmacy change rather than adjacent cleanup or generated collateral.
triage.fhir_spec_impact: The commit changes only source/medicationknowledge/structuredefinition-MedicationKnowledge.xml, an editor-owned conformance source. The added invariant and condition references change validation/conformance behavior for MedicationKnowledge.indicationGuideline, and the added example binding changes the terminology metadata rendered and distributed for MedicationKnowledge.indicationGuideline.dosingGuideline.treatmentIntent.
triage.recommended_reviewer_action: Keep this as the Jira-backed MedicationKnowledge fix. Review the exact FHIRPath and SNOMED implicit value set URI for technical correctness, but there is no generated-file or subset concern in this commit.

jira_evidence.explanation: The published Pharmacy resolution specifically required treatmentIntent, an indication-required constraint when treatmentIntent is present, and an example binding to children of SNOMED CT 262202000; this commit applies the constraint and binding that remained missing after the element was added.

This published related MedicationKnowledge decision states that the model was inverted and AdministrationGuideline became DosingGuideline under IndicationGuideline, supporting the current target path for the FHIR-30092 requirement.

This published decision pulled indication out of administrationGuideline and made the guideline a child of indication, which explains why the older Jira wording maps to MedicationKnowledge.indicationGuideline in the current model.

This later no-change MedicationRequest issue noted MedicationKnowledge treatmentIntent was not yet bound, but it did not supersede or narrow the approved MedicationKnowledge requirement from FHIR-30092.

caveats: The Jira resolution used the older administrationGuideline name; the related published refactoring decisions and Pharmacy minutes support applying the missing pieces on indicationGuideline.dosingGuideline.treatmentIntent today.
The commit touches only the authoritative MedicationKnowledge StructureDefinition and no hard-avoid generated, derived, or layout-only files.

commits.author: Josh Mandel
commits.subject: FHIR-29114: Clarify Procedure.supportingInfo as an element

triage.category_rationale: FHIR-29114 resolved to remove extension treatment and add Procedure.supportingInfo to the base Procedure resource as 0..* Reference(Any), with a definition for other patient-record resources relevant to the procedure. The current Procedure StructureDefinition has the J#29114 element with the approved short text, cardinality, and reference type, but its definition still says "This extension should not be used," directly conflicting with the resolved base-element change and the Jira comment that the workflow supportingInfo extension did not apply to Procedure. Because source/procedure/structuredefinition-Procedure.xml is the authoritative Procedure conformance source, the stale wording is carried into current ElementDefinition text and rendered/conformance output. Changing only "This extension" to "This element" is the narrow source edit needed to complete the Jira application, not generated collateral, optional consistency work, or a later policy change.
triage.fhir_spec_impact: The changed file is the authoritative StructureDefinition XML for Procedure. Its ElementDefinition.definition text is used for the current Procedure specification and conformance artifact, so the stale extension wording misdescribes a base element in reader-visible and machine-distributed content.
triage.recommended_reviewer_action: Keep this as the Jira-backed source fix for FHIR-29114. No generated, layout-only, or hard-avoid file is part of the actual commit.

jira_evidence.explanation: The Published/Persuasive Patient Care resolution required adding supportingInfo to the base Procedure resource as 0..* Reference(Any) and no longer treating it as a Procedure extension; the comments also clarify the workflow supportingInfo extension did not apply to Procedure. That directly requires the base element definition not to call itself an extension.
FHIR-26622 was bundled into the same historical source commit but concerned a Procedure.report search parameter, not Procedure.supportingInfo. It does not justify this wording change.

caveats: The commit message discusses a Procedure SVG tooltip, but the actual reviewed commit only changes source/procedure/structuredefinition-Procedure.xml.

commits.author: Josh Mandel

The stale spelling affects current rendered/conformance element metadata by listing an invalid TitleType code for `ResearchStudy.label.type` even though the element is bound to the THO TitleType value set.

jira_evidence.explanation: The resolution approved the concrete TitleType code list containing `autotranslated` and changed the duplicate identifier code to `duplicate-uid`; this directly requires active FHIR source surfaces using that TitleType list not to publish `auto-translated`.

The issue records broader Citation terminology requests and notes that TitleType concepts were handled through other trackers, supporting FHIR-32975 as the concrete TitleType decision rather than independently requiring this edit.
The later terminology migration explains why the current core fix should be limited to active ResearchStudy references and should not edit or recreate removed core CodeSystem files.

commits.author: Josh Mandel
commits.subject: FHIR-36046: Fix Appointment recurrence element metadata
commits.summary: Corrected narrow Appointment recurrence StructureDefinition metadata defects left after the R5 recurring appointments application.

triage.reviewer_summary: Jira-backed missed application: FHIR-36046 approved the recurring Appointment model, but the authoritative Appointment StructureDefinition still had narrow metadata defects in the recurrence elements. This commit fixes the malformed recurrenceTemplate id, the recurrenceType binding description, and a broken monthly recurrence element reference without changing the approved model.
triage.category_rationale: FHIR-36046 was Published/Persuasive for R5 and resolved to apply the recurring appointments proposal to Appointment and AppointmentResponse, including an Appointment recurrence template, a recurrenceType representing recurrence frequency, a separate timezone element, and monthly day-of-week recurrence tied to the nth week of the month. The current Appointment StructureDefinition incompletely applies that approved model: Appointment.recurrenceTemplate has an element id with a trailing space rather than the actual path, Appointment.recurrenceTemplate.recurrenceType carries the timezone binding description even though timezone is a separate element, and Appointment.recurrenceTemplate.monthlyTemplate.dayOfWeek points to a non-existent Appointment.recurrenceTemplate.monthly.nthWeek path instead of the implemented nthWeekOfMonth element. Because this XML is the authoritative conformance source for Appointment, the defects flow into generated StructureDefinition metadata and rendered element/binding/comment text. The proposed edit is required to finish the approved recurrence application because it corrects only contradictory or malformed metadata on elements introduced for that Jira, rather than adding adjacent cleanup or a later recurrence policy change.
triage.fhir_spec_impact: source/appointment/structuredefinition-Appointment.xml is the current conformance source for Appointment. The stale metadata would affect generated Appointment StructureDefinition output and rendered element details as a malformed ElementDefinition id, an incorrect binding description that describes timezone instead of recurrence frequency, and a broken local reference in monthly recurrence guidance.
triage.recommended_reviewer_action: Keep this as a Jira-backed source fix for FHIR-36046. Review any later recurrence datatype, guidance, or search-parameter changes under their own issues rather than folding them into this narrow metadata correction.

jira_evidence.explanation: The Published/Persuasive resolution required applying the recurring Appointment proposal to Appointment and AppointmentResponse. The accepted proposal defines recurrenceTemplate as the recurrence detail container, recurrenceType as the frequency of recurrence, timezone as a distinct template element, and monthly day-of-week recurrence in relation to the nth week; the changed metadata is part of correctly representing those approved elements in the Appointment StructureDefinition.

This later Applied issue added recurrence-related Appointment search parameters. It does not justify the metadata corrections here, but it confirms the recurrence model remains active and that search-parameter work is a separate concern.

triage.tooling_recommendation: Consider adding a consistency check that flags ElementDefinition ids that do not match paths and comments that reference non-existent local element paths, since these defects can survive in authoritative conformance source.

commits.author: Josh Mandel
commits.subject: FHIR-28235: Align Communication scope timing wording
commits.summary: Aligned the remaining Communication Scope and Usage sentence with the final process-initiated wording approved for FHIR-28235.

triage.reviewer_summary: Jira-backed missed application: FHIR-28235 approved replacing Communication wording that treated merely planned communications as in scope, but the Scope and Usage paragraph still retained that older sentence. This commit updates the editor-owned Communication introduction narrative to the approved process-initiated timing rule.
triage.category_rationale: FHIR-28235 was Applied/Persuasive with Modification and resolved to say that Communication records a communication that has occurred or where the communication process has at least initiated, while also allowing actual communication flow in some use cases. The earlier application updated the Communication Boundaries and Relationships wording but missed the Scope and Usage sentence in source/communication/communication-introduction.xml, which still said the resource could be a record even if communication was planned or had failed. That introduction file is the current Communication resource narrative, so the missed sentence creates reader-visible scope guidance that conflicts with the approved timing rule. Replacing the stale planned/failed sentence with the process-initiated wording is required to complete the Jira application rather than optional cleanup.
triage.fhir_spec_impact: The changed file is the Communication resource introduction narrative, so the sentence affects rendered scope guidance for when Communication is appropriate. It is not generated collateral or an ignored source residue; it corrects current reader-visible specification text.
triage.recommended_reviewer_action: Keep the source fix as the Jira-backed completion of FHIR-28235 on the Communication narrative page.

jira_evidence.explanation: The Applied/Persuasive with Modification resolution gives the concrete replacement concept: Communication is a record of a communication that has occurred or where the communication process has at least initiated, and it may represent actual flow in some use cases. The changed Scope and Usage sentence is the same planned/failed wording identified in the issue request.

This Applied/Persuasive with Modification issue approved related Communication wording that supports correspondence co-occurring with an interaction and allows actual-flow use cases. FHIR-28235 supplies the later narrowed timing phrase used by this commit.

This earlier Applied issue touched related Communication boundary language and explains the history of adding future-tense wording, but FHIR-28235 is the decision that narrowed the active timing guidance away from merely planned communications.

caveats: No hard-avoid generated or SVG files are part of this commit; the only changed file is editor-owned Communication narrative source.

commits.author: Josh Mandel
commits.subject: FHIR-47287: Clarify Subscription status diagram labels
commits.summary: Completed the applied Subscriptions diagram clarification by replacing remaining Subscription-resource status shorthand labels with Subscription.status in the build-scoped workflow and error-recovery diagrams.

triage.reviewer_summary: Jira-backed missed application: FHIR-47287 expressly required Subscription workflow diagram shorthand status labels to say Subscription.status, and three current Subscription diagram sources still used bare status wording for Subscription resource status changes.
triage.category_rationale: FHIR-47287 resolved to update short-hand references to status in diagrams to Subscription.status, specifically because labels such as status=active were ambiguous when they meant the Subscription resource status. The prior implementation updated some Subscription workflow labels but left the same required wording unapplied in images/subscriptions/subscription-workflow-general.plantuml, subscription-error-missing-event.plantuml, and subscription-error-no-communication.plantuml. Those PlantUML files are the source for Subscriptions diagrams embedded from source/subscriptions.html and published as SVGs, so stale labels in these sources correspond to stale reader-visible diagram content when the diagrams are generated. The edit is required to finish the Jira application because each changed label is exactly a remaining Subscription resource status transition covered by the resolution, not a broader diagram cleanup or a change to the separate SubscriptionStatus resource wording.
triage.fhir_spec_impact: The changed files are diagram sources for current Subscriptions page diagrams. The rendered specification uses the generated/published SVGs, so the source fix should be paired with normal SVG regeneration; without that, the checked-in output can remain stale even though the editor-owned diagram source is corrected.
triage.recommended_reviewer_action: Keep the PlantUML source changes as the Jira-backed fix and regenerate the published SVG diagrams through the normal diagram tooling rather than hand-editing generated SVG output.

jira_evidence.explanation: The issue description requested replacing ambiguous Subscriptions workflow labels such as status=active with Subscription.status=active, and the resolution says to update short-hand references to status in diagrams to Subscription.status.

This earlier Subscriptions documentation work relates to the error-recovery diagrams where two remaining bare Subscription status labels appeared, but it is not the decision requiring this wording change.
This separate Subscription diagram cleanup addressed Bundle.type values and does not justify the Subscription.status label change.

triage.tooling_recommendation: Use or add a diagram-source synchronization check so PlantUML label changes that affect published diagrams require regenerated SVGs and source/output drift is caught.
caveats: This commit intentionally keeps only the editor-owned PlantUML source changes; the corresponding SVG files are generated diagram output and should be regenerated separately.
The SubscriptionStatus.status label in the no-communication diagram is outside this fix because it refers to the SubscriptionStatus resource, not Subscription.status.

commits.author: Josh Mandel
commits.subject: FHIR-22657: Restore MoneyQuantity as Quantity constraint
commits.summary: Restored the applied FHIR-22657 datatype-page change so MoneyQuantity is listed as the second Quantity constraint while Money remains a datatype.

triage.reviewer_summary: Jira-backed missed application: FHIR-22657 explicitly required the datatype page to state that Quantity has two constraints and to list MoneyQuantity in the Quantity constraints table. This commit restores that approved reader-visible datatype-page content after a later edit regressed the placement.
triage.category_rationale: FHIR-22657 was Published as Persuasive with Modification and concretely required changing the Quantity variations sentence from one constraint to two constraints and adding MoneyQuantity to the table immediately following that sentence. The current source/datatypes.html surface still conflicted with that resolution by saying there was only one Quantity constraint, omitting MoneyQuantity from the Quantity constraints table, and duplicating the MoneyQuantity formal-definition table under the Money alternate-representation section. Because source/datatypes.html is the editor-owned source for the rendered datatype page, this affects current reader-visible datatype documentation about Quantity, Money, and MoneyQuantity. Moving MoneyQuantity into the Quantity constraints table, pluralizing the explanatory note, and leaving the Money section as prose are required to complete the Jira application rather than optional consistency cleanup.
triage.fhir_spec_impact: The changed file is active datatype-page source and renders guidance about Quantity specializations and constraints. Before this commit, the rendered datatype documentation incorrectly described only one Quantity constraint and did not present MoneyQuantity where the approved resolution required it; the commit corrects that current reader-visible source without touching generated artifacts or hard-avoid files.
triage.recommended_reviewer_action: Keep this as a Jira-backed source fix for FHIR-22657 and review the whole commit as the restored datatype-page application of the approved resolution.

jira_evidence.explanation: The Published/Persuasive with Modification resolution for the FHIR-core datatypes page explicitly says to change the Quantity variations line to state there are two constraints on Quantity and to add MoneyQuantity to the table immediately following that line. That directly requires the source/datatypes.html update made here.

caveats: Historical source evidence indicates FHIR-22657 had previously been applied and a later RatioRange datatype edit reintroduced the stale placement, so this is a restoration rather than a new policy change.
The commit touches only source/datatypes.html, not generated artifacts, SVGs, or other editor-avoided files.

commits.author: Josh Mandel

The commit applies that missing guidance to the current patientCharacteristic element.

commits.author: Josh Mandel

commits.author: Josh Mandel

No generated, derived, SVG, or other hard-avoid files are included in this commit.

commits.author: Josh Mandel
commits.subject: FHIR-28217: Align Goal acceptance participant wording
commits.summary: Aligned active Goal acceptance wording with the applied participant model and removed stale individual-only/typo wording.

The current source does contain stale individual-only wording and a malformed participant definition in an authoritative StructureDefinition, so the proposed direction is a real current-spec correction. However, this commit goes beyond the exact resolved text by changing the backbone short, status definition, and priority short, and by replacing the Jira's specified individual-or-organization phrase with broader participant wording that also reflects later Group context. Because reviewer feedback says this needs to be revisited with a WG vote, the whole commit should not be treated as already required by the existing Jira record without WG confirmation of the exact wording.
triage.fhir_spec_impact: source/goal/structuredefinition-Goal.xml is the authoritative Goal StructureDefinition. These short and definition strings are rendered in the specification and carried into generated conformance metadata, so stale references to an individual can misdescribe the current participant-based acceptance model; this is not merely repository hygiene.
triage.recommended_reviewer_action: Bring the wording back to Patient Care or a follow-up Jira to confirm the exact text to use for Goal.acceptance, Goal.acceptance.participant, Goal.acceptance.status, and Goal.acceptance.priority. If approved, apply the authoritative XML source change; do not rely on this as a clean already-voted wording application without that confirmation.

jira_evidence.explanation: The resolution explicitly required renaming Goal.acceptance.individual to Goal.acceptance.participant, adding PractitionerRole, CareTeam, and Organization targets, and updating the participant description/definition to 'Individual or organization whose acceptance is reflected.' That supports removing individual-only wording, but it does not explicitly approve the exact broader wording used here for the backbone, status, and priority surfaces.

The current source marks Goal.acceptance.participant with J#48366 and includes Group as a target, supporting the conclusion that current wording should not be limited to a single individual. It is supporting context for participant-neutral text, not by itself proof that this whole wording update was already resolved under FHIR-28217.
This earlier Goal.source issue provides related participant/source context, but it did not decide the Goal.acceptance wording changed in this commit.

triage.tooling_recommendation: Consider a QA check that flags descriptions and shorts retaining old actor terms after an element rename or target-profile expansion, so these inconsistencies are surfaced for WG review instead of remaining as silent conformance text drift.
caveats: Human review for this item says to revisit with a WG vote, which is strong evidence against treating the whole commit as already approved wording cleanup.

commits.subject: FHIR-49736: Remove stale vital signs component summary requirements
commits.summary: Removed stale component-specific mandatory-requirement summary text from the Vital Signs Base Profile now that component Must Support is confined to the Blood Pressure profile.

triage.reviewer_summary: This is a real Vital Signs StructureDefinition summary fix, but it should be reviewed as a subset/attribution cleanup rather than a clean single-ticket application. The component mandatory-summary removals are backed by FHIR-49736 and FHIR-47136, while the same XML string replacement also cleans up older `Observation.related.target`/hasMember summary wording that is not specifically required by those resolutions.
triage.category_rationale: FHIR-49736 resolved that Must Support should be removed from `Observation.component` and its sub-elements in the Vital Signs Base Profile and moved to the Blood Pressure profile; FHIR-47136 is the earlier applied issue for the same behavior. The missed application is clear for the base-profile summary extensions that still described `Observation.component.code` and `Observation.component.valueQuantity`/`Observation.component.dataAbsentReason` as mandatory requirements even after the formal base differential stopped marking those component elements Must Support and the Blood Pressure profile carried the component requirements. Those summary extensions are current StructureDefinition metadata, so stale mandatory text affects profile summary/conformance presentation and should be removed. However, the edit also removes `Observation.related.target` mandatory-summary text and changes the profile-summary value/component/hasMember sentence; those appear to be legitimate current summary cleanup, but they are not concretely required by the component Must Support resolutions. The whole commit therefore needs a subset or cleanup-ticket path rather than being treated as entirely Jira-backed.
triage.fhir_spec_impact: The changed file is the authoritative Vital Signs Base Profile StructureDefinition XML. Its `structuredefinition-summary` and `profile-summary` extension values are used as profile summary/conformance metadata, so the stale component-specific mandatory paragraphs can mislead readers and downstream consumers even though the formal differential is already aligned. The `Observation.related.target`/hasMember wording cleanup also affects the same metadata surface, but its Jira basis is not established by the component Must Support issues.
triage.recommended_reviewer_action: Keep the FHIR-49736/FHIR-47136-backed removal of component sub-element mandatory-summary requirements. If retaining the `Observation.related.target`/hasMember cleanup in the same patch, cover it with a small cleanup or rollup issue, or split it so the component Must Support reconciliation remains cleanly attributable.

jira_evidence.explanation: The resolution specifically required removing Must Support from `Observation.component` in the Vital Signs Base Profile, including component sub-elements, and moving that requirement to the Blood Pressure profile. That directly supports removing base-profile summary text that still presents component sub-elements as mandatory, but it does not specifically require the `Observation.related.target`/hasMember cleanup.

This earlier applied OO issue resolved the same model change: remove `Observation.component` Must Support from non-Blood Pressure vital signs profiles and add it to Blood Pressure. Its application history explains why the differential is already corrected while the base summary extensions were left stale.

This issue concerned the `Observation.component.valueQuantity` binding and later comments say the FHIR-47136 work satisfied it. It does not independently require the summary text changes in this commit.

triage.tooling_recommendation: Consider a profile-summary consistency check that flags mandatory-summary text referencing removed/renamed elements or elements no longer marked Must Support in the corresponding profile.
caveats: The formal Vital Signs Base Profile differential and Blood Pressure profile constraints were already aligned; this change addresses stale summary metadata.
The component sub-element mandatory-summary removals are the clearly ticket-backed subset.
The `Observation.related.target`/hasMember wording is likely a useful current cleanup, but should be covered by a cleanup/rollup issue or explicitly accepted as part of this patch.

commits.author: Josh Mandel

This commit corrects only source/fhir.ini so migration/change reporting recognizes those paths as moves.
triage.category_rationale: FHIR-46492 was an Applied FHIR-core resolution requiring SubscriptionTopic.resourceTrigger and SubscriptionTopic.eventTrigger to collapse into a single SubscriptionTopic.trigger backbone, with canFilterBy and notificationShape defined under each trigger, plus optional event tagging in Subscription and SubscriptionStatus. The primary StructureDefinition changes are already present, but source/fhir.ini's active [r5-r6-changes] metadata still left SubscriptionTopic.eventTrigger, eventTrigger.description, eventTrigger.event, eventTrigger.resource, notificationShape.include, resourceTrigger.description, resourceTrigger.resource, and resourceTrigger.supportedInteraction blank or commented rather than mapped with @new-name to their R6 trigger locations; the same file says moved or renamed backbone children must be marked this way. That stale metadata affects the current rendered/version-change information by misclassifying Jira-required moves as deletions or unrelated additions. The edit is required to finish the Jira application because it updates exactly the missing move mappings for the approved trigger collapse and does not include generated, avoided, or adjacent cleanup files.
triage.fhir_spec_impact: The current SubscriptionTopic, Subscription, and SubscriptionStatus conformance resources already reflect the approved R6 model. The remaining impact is source/fhir.ini's R5-to-R6 change metadata, an editor-owned build input for version/migration reporting; stale blank or commented mappings would make the current spec's change view inaccurate for the moved SubscriptionTopic trigger elements.
triage.recommended_reviewer_action: Keep this as the Jira-backed fix to the SubscriptionTopic R5-to-R6 change metadata for FHIR-46492.

jira_evidence.explanation: The Applied FHIR-core resolution specifically required collapsing SubscriptionTopic.resourceTrigger and SubscriptionTopic.eventTrigger into SubscriptionTopic.trigger, moving canFilterBy and notificationShape under trigger, and adding related optional event-tagging elements. The corrected fhir.ini entries are the version-change mappings for those required SubscriptionTopic moves.

This subscriptions backport issue supplied the same design rationale to merge event/resource triggers and add notification event tagging. It supports the interpretation of the model change, while FHIR-46492 is the direct core attribution for this source update.

The missed application is the current source/security.html summary checklist line, which still recommended OAuth for web-centric authentication even though the detailed Authentication section had already gained OpenID Connect guidance. triage.fhir_spec_impact: source/security.html is rendered narrative for the FHIR security page. jira_evidence.explanation: The Published/Persuasive with Modification resolution explicitly says to add to the checklist a recommendation to use OpenID Connect, or another suitable authentication protocol, to verify end-user identity where needed, and to reference SMART on FHIR, UMA, and HEART. commits.author: Josh Mandel
commits.subject: FHIR-17987: Make PaymentNotice amount optional
commits.summary: Changed the active PaymentNotice StructureDefinition so PaymentNotice.amount is optional (0..1) instead of mandatory (1..1).

triage.reviewer_summary: Jira-backed missed application: FHIR-17987 specifically requested PaymentNotice.amount as 0..1 Money, but the current PaymentNotice StructureDefinition still made the element mandatory. This commit corrects the authoritative cardinality to optional without touching generated or collateral files.
triage.category_rationale: FHIR-17987 was Published/Persuasive and its request text concretely required adding PaymentNotice.amount as 0..1 Money for the amount of the payment. The element was added, but the application used min 1, and that incorrect required cardinality remains in source/paymentnotice/structuredefinition-PaymentNotice.xml. Because this StructureDefinition is the authoritative conformance source for PaymentNotice, the stale min value affects generated conformance output and validation expectations by requiring amount where the resolved Jira made it optional. Changing only PaymentNotice.amount min from 1 to 0 is necessary to complete that Jira application; it is not adjacent cleanup, generated-file synchronization, or an unrelated editorial improvement.
triage.fhir_spec_impact: The changed file is the editor-owned PaymentNotice StructureDefinition, so the min cardinality is part of current conformance output and validator behavior for PaymentNotice.amount. Leaving it at 1..1 would continue to make amount mandatory despite the resolved optional 0..1 Jira request.
triage.recommended_reviewer_action: Keep this as the Jira-backed cardinality fix for PaymentNotice.amount.

jira_evidence.explanation: The Published/Persuasive request says to add 'amount 0..1 Money' for PaymentNotice, which directly specifies both the element and optional cardinality corrected by this commit.

This related PaymentNotice issue required identifier, created, paymentDate, payment, payee, and amount to be summary fields; it supports the same element family but does not alter the 0..1 cardinality required by FHIR-17987.
This related PaymentNotice cardinality issue made status, patient, created, and paymentStatus 1..1; it did not list amount and therefore does not justify keeping PaymentNotice.amount mandatory.

commits.author: Josh Mandel

FHIR-43696 later required adding RelativeTime as an allowed timing[x] type in ActivityDefinition and PlanDefinition, leaving those current comments incomplete because they still explain the other timing choices but not RelativeTime. That makes the wording a reasonable current conformance-comment fix, but the recorded RelativeTime resolution only says to add the datatype option, and FHIR-29799 did not address RelativeTime, so this should not be treated as a clean Jira-backed missed application without better attribution or an explicit editorial/WG path.
triage.fhir_spec_impact: The changed files are authoritative StructureDefinition XML for active resources. jira_evidence.explanation: The resolution agreed to clarify timing usages in PlanDefinition and ActivityDefinition, and the issue text specifically called out Range and Duration semantics. This earlier change removed dateTime and Period from definitional timing choices and appears to have introduced the existing explanatory comments for Age, Duration, Range, and Timing. This later Applied/Persuasive issue required adding RelativeTime as an option in ActivityDefinition.timing[x] and PlanDefinition.action.timing[x]. It is the strongest context for the current omission, but its recorded resolution does not specifically require updating the explanatory comments, so it is not enough by itself for a clean Jira-backed missed-application finding.

triage.tooling_recommendation: Consider a consistency check for choice-type comments that enumerate datatype-specific meanings, so adding a new choice prompts editors to review related explanatory comments.
caveats: The current source impact is real because StructureDefinition comments are rendered/conformance content, but the Jira chain does not prove that this exact wording was required by an already approved resolution.
FHIR-43696 is the more relevant attribution than FHIR-29799 for RelativeTime, but reviewers may still prefer a new small clarification issue if they want explicit approval for comment wording.

commits.summary: Completed the applied Search page clarification for non-Reference references by removing stale prohibitive prose and adding the missing canonical chaining/navigation details.

triage.reviewer_summary: Jira-backed missed application: FHIR-45252 explicitly approved Search page clarifications for chaining, includes, reverse includes, the [type] modifier, canonical references, and the duplicated Canonical Identifiers heading. This commit completes those approved narrative and navigation changes in the active Search page source.
triage.category_rationale: FHIR-45252 was resolved Persuasive with the instruction to make the proposed Search page changes: replace prohibitive non-Reference reference-search language with 'not defined' plus server discretion, add canonical chaining and include guidance with a QuestionnaireResponse-to-Questionnaire example, update the [type] modifier note, advertise include/revInclude support through CapabilityStatement text, and fix the duplicated Canonical Identifiers heading. The current source still retained the old [type] external-reference note, 'not supported/cannot' language for non-Reference reference chaining/includes/reverse includes, a resource-identifier section mislabeled under the canonical identifier anchor, a missing Canonical References local TOC entry, and incomplete canonical chaining notes/example. Those are active source/search.html narrative surfaces, so they render as reader-facing search semantics and page navigation. The edit is required to complete the approved application because it applies the exact requested prose, example, and heading/anchor corrections without turning optional canonical resolution into a new mandatory rule.
triage.fhir_spec_impact: source/search.html is the authoritative narrative for the rendered Search page. The stale text incorrectly told readers that chaining, includes, and reverse includes for canonical or other non-Reference references were unsupported or impossible, while the approved clarification says the base specification does not define them but servers may support them with implementation-specific resolution behavior; the heading, anchor, and TOC fixes also affect rendered navigation.
triage.recommended_reviewer_action: Keep this as the FHIR-45252-backed Search page fix. It should be reviewed as completion of an already-approved clarification, not as a new policy change requiring a separate vote.

jira_evidence.explanation: The Applied/Persuasive resolution says to make the proposed Search page changes. The proposal names the exact stale paragraphs and replacements for non-Reference reference chaining/include/revInclude behavior, canonical chaining notes and example, [type] modifier restrictions, Canonical References include text, CapabilityStatement advertising guidance, and the duplicated Canonical Identifiers heading fix.

FHIR-43073 earlier clarified reference-search terminology and explains why this area of source/search.html was being refined, but it is not the decision that requires the canonical chaining/include clarification made here.

commits.author: Josh Mandel
commits.subject: FHIR-30343: Clarify $validate-code abstract default
commits.summary: Completed the published FHIR-30343 correction by updating the active CodeSystem and ValueSet $validate-code abstract parameter documentation.

triage.reviewer_summary: Jira-backed missed application: FHIR-30343 explicitly required the CodeSystem and ValueSet $validate-code abstract input documentation to say that an omitted parameter behaves like abstract=true and to correct the object-oriented abstract-terminology sentence. The active CodeSystem operation definition still lacked that approved omitted-parameter behavior and stale wording, while the ValueSet operation definition retained the remaining object-orientated spelling in the same approved sentence.
triage.category_rationale: FHIR-30343 is the responsible Published/Persuasive Vocabulary decision for FHIR-core CodeSystem and ValueSet. Its concrete resolution changed the abstract input documentation from "If this parameter has a value of true" to "If this parameter has a value of true or the parameter is omitted" and added that false means abstract codes are not valid; it also changed the later terminology sentence to "object-oriented theory where 'abstract' entities are never instantiated." The missed application is specific: the current CodeSystem OperationDefinition still documented only abstract=true, not omitted-as-true, and retained stale object-oriented wording, while the ValueSet OperationDefinition still used the object-orientated spelling in that Jira-approved sentence. These XML files are authoritative active OperationDefinition source for the current $validate-code operations, so the parameter documentation is rendered and distributed as operation-definition content. The edit is necessary to finish the approved application because it updates exactly the remaining CodeSystem and ValueSet operation-definition text named by the Jira, rather than generated collateral, optional consistency work, or unrelated cleanup.
triage.fhir_spec_impact: The changed files are authoritative OperationDefinition source for the CodeSystem and ValueSet $validate-code operations. Without the CodeSystem change, current published operation documentation would continue to omit the approved rule that absence of the abstract parameter is equivalent to abstract=true; the ValueSet spelling correction affects the rendered parameter documentation for the same approved abstract-terminology sentence.
triage.recommended_reviewer_action: Keep the commit as the Jira-backed source fix for FHIR-30343; no subset omission, regeneration-only handling, or new WG path is indicated.

jira_evidence.explanation: The issue is Published/Persuasive for FHIR-core CodeSystem and ValueSet and explicitly requires the $validate-code abstract parameter documentation to state that true or omission permits abstract codes, that false excludes them, and that the object-oriented abstract-entities sentence be corrected.

This older published issue established broader clarification text for the CodeSystem abstract parameter, but it does not replace FHIR-30343 as the direct R5 decision requiring omitted-parameter behavior.

This older published CodeSystem issue confirms the same abstract-parameter wording area and typo history; it is background because FHIR-30343 is the later decision that specifically covers the omitted-parameter default.
This older CodeSystem typo issue is consistent with correcting the same documentation area, but FHIR-30343 independently contains the wording correction applied here.

commits.author: Josh Mandel
commits.subject: FHIR-28578: Correct Appointment invariant source metadata
commits.summary: Corrected the source metadata on the already-present Appointment app-5 start/end ordering invariant.

triage.reviewer_summary: Jira-backed missed application: FHIR-28578 required an Appointment start/end ordering invariant, and the active constraint was added with a copied Questionnaire source canonical. This one-line update corrects the authoritative Appointment StructureDefinition metadata to identify Appointment as the declaring StructureDefinition.
triage.category_rationale: FHIR-28578 was a Published/Persuasive Patient Administration resolution requiring an Appointment invariant to ensure the start date is before or equal to the end date when both are provided. The current Appointment StructureDefinition contains that app-5 invariant and attaches it to Appointment.start and Appointment.end, but the constraint source still names http://hl7.org/fhir/StructureDefinition/Questionnaire, which conflicts with the Appointment-local invariant approved by the Jira. Because this XML is the authoritative current conformance source for Appointment, the stale canonical propagates incorrect metadata for the active invariant. Changing the source canonical to http://hl7.org/fhir/StructureDefinition/Appointment is required to complete the approved Appointment invariant application; it is not generated collateral, optional cleanup, or an unrelated consistency edit.
triage.fhir_spec_impact: The changed file is the authoritative Appointment StructureDefinition XML. The invariant expression is already present, but the current conformance metadata identifies the active Appointment app-5 constraint as sourced from Questionnaire, so generated StructureDefinition content and downstream consumers can misidentify the origin of the rule until this is corrected.
triage.recommended_reviewer_action: Keep this as the Jira-backed correction for the Appointment invariant metadata approved under FHIR-28578.

jira_evidence.explanation: The resolution required adding an Appointment invariant so Appointment.end is not before Appointment.start when both values are provided. The implementation added the rule but left the constraint source canonical copied from Questionnaire, so the approved Appointment invariant was not fully applied in the authoritative metadata.

This broader invariant-cleanup issue asked for specific tracker items where invariant metadata was wrong; it does not itself require this Appointment edit, but it supports treating this as a specific issue-backed invariant metadata correction.

A later recurring-appointments change touched Appointment content and left the copied Questionnaire canonical unchanged. It does not supersede or narrow the FHIR-28578 start/end invariant requirement.

triage.tooling_recommendation: A QA check could flag resource-local constraints whose source canonical names an unrelated StructureDefinition.

This related Coverage issue concerned adding a boundaries section and does not address the workflow Event statement or link label.

triage.recommended_reviewer_action: Keep this as the Jira-backed source fix for FHIR-30757. No generated diagram, derived file, terminology-code reassignment, or unrelated binding hunk is included.

commits.author: Josh Mandel
commits.subject: FHIR-13504: Restore OperationOutcome entity description example
commits.summary: Restored the AuditEvent transaction-failure example so the entity that references the contained OperationOutcome also includes entity.description.

triage.reviewer_summary: Jira-backed missed application. FHIR-13504 specifically directed AuditEvent guidance and an example to record an OperationOutcome as an AuditEvent.entity with a reference and description; the current transaction-failure example still referenced the contained OperationOutcome but omitted entity.description.
triage.category_rationale: FHIR-13504 resolved that OperationOutcome evidence for a FHIR transaction should be represented on AuditEvent by recording the OperationOutcome as an AuditEvent.entity, with a reference to the OperationOutcome, entity.description explaining why it was included, and an example demonstrating that pattern. The current AuditEvent notes still tell readers to use entity.what for the OperationOutcome reference and entity.description for why the OperationOutcome was included, and they link to the transaction-failure example, but that example had only entity.what.reference/display and no entity.description. The example is an editor-owned AuditEvent example XML file, and the added field is a valid AuditEvent.entity.description element, so the correction changes the visible/distributed example that illustrates the current AuditEvent guidance. Adding the description is required to complete the FHIR-13504 application while respecting the later FHIR-32467 removal of entity.type; it is not generated collateral, optional consistency work, or a separate policy change.
triage.fhir_spec_impact: The changed file is an AuditEvent example source file used to illustrate transaction failure with a contained OperationOutcome and linked from the AuditEvent notes. Restoring entity.description changes the current example content readers and implementers see, bringing it back into alignment with the narrative guidance and the Jira-required example semantics.
triage.recommended_reviewer_action: Keep this as a Jira-backed fix to the AuditEvent OperationOutcome example. Do not reintroduce entity.type for this issue, because that older part of the STU3 wording was superseded by the later AuditEvent.entity.type removal.

jira_evidence.explanation: The published Not Persuasive with Modification resolution required an AuditEvent section explaining how to encode an OperationOutcome as evidence of a FHIR transaction, recording it as AuditEvent.entity with a reference to the OperationOutcome and entity.description describing why it was included, plus an example.

The later published Persuasive resolution removed AuditEvent.entity.type as redundant with entity.what, which explains why the current fix should restore only entity.description while preserving the current entity.what reference form.

caveats: The older entity.type part of the STU3 wording should remain omitted because later AuditEvent model changes intentionally removed that element.

commits.author: Josh Mandel
commits.subject: FHIR-48110: Align BodyStructure morphology examples
commits.summary: Completed the applied FHIR-48110 morphology move by fixing active BodyStructure examples and stale definition/diagram wording while preserving the approved 0..1 ServiceRequest.bodyStructure cardinality.

triage.reviewer_summary: Jira-backed missed application: FHIR-48110 rejected increasing ServiceRequest.bodyStructure cardinality and instead required morphology to move under BodyStructure.includedStructure. This commit completes that approved BodyStructure change on editor-owned XML source by moving stale example morphology values to the new element and correcting the moved element definition.
triage.category_rationale: The responsible resolution is FHIR-48110, which specifically required keeping ServiceRequest.bodyStructure at 0..1 and making morphology part of BodyStructure.includedStructure 0..1. The current BodyStructure source still missed that application in two ways: active BodyStructure examples retained morphology as a removed root child, and BodyStructure.includedStructure.morphology still defined the element as if it described the body structure at BodyStructure.location. Those missed surfaces affect current specification content because the StructureDefinition definition is authoritative rendered/conformance text, and the examples' intended morphology values are lost from generated example output when left at the removed root path. Moving the example values under includedStructure and updating the definition are required to complete the approved morphology move rather than adjacent cleanup or a new policy change.
triage.fhir_spec_impact: source/bodystructure/structuredefinition-BodyStructure.xml is authoritative conformance source and its definition text is rendered for BodyStructure.includedStructure.morphology. The two BodyStructure example XML files are active examples; before this edit their root-level morphology content no longer matched the current model and the generated examples omitted the morphology values instead of showing valid includedStructure.morphology content.
triage.recommended_reviewer_action: Keep this as the Jira-backed BodyStructure completion for FHIR-48110. Review it narrowly as finishing the approved morphology move, not as reopening the rejected request to make ServiceRequest.bodyStructure repeat.

jira_evidence.explanation: The Applied / Not Persuasive with Modification resolution explicitly says not to change ServiceRequest.bodyStructure from 0..1 and instead to make morphology part of BodyStructure.includedStructure 0..1. That concrete decision requires current BodyStructure source surfaces that used or described the old root morphology location to be moved or corrected.

This later Patient Care issue is described as aligning Procedure.bodyStructure back to 0..1 after FHIR-48110. It supports preserving the 0..1 cardinality outcome but is not the direct basis for the BodyStructure example and definition edits in this commit.

FHIR-48110 references this earlier Procedure cardinality decision family. It explains the related Procedure history but does not replace FHIR-48110 as the responsible resolution for the BodyStructure morphology move.

triage.tooling_recommendation: Add or tighten QA warnings when active example source contains removed elements that the publisher silently drops, because that can hide lost example content after structural changes.
caveats: The actual commit changes only editor-owned XML files; it does not include the checked-in BodyStructure SVG mentioned in some surrounding history.
The example-source impact depends on the morphology values being preserved as valid example content after the structural move, not merely on cleaning unknown root elements.

commits.author: Josh Mandel

Rewording the sentence to say the server might populate the element when data is received or when crafting a response instance is required to complete the same Jira application and does not add adjacent search, extension, generated, or diagram changes.

triage.recommended_reviewer_action: Keep the source edit as the Jira-backed completion of FHIR-45047. Handle any future computable disclosure of lastUpdated guarantees, extension work, or search-parameter wording changes under a separate issue.

This related lastUpdated/facade discussion provides background for the false-positive/false-negative semantics, but the narrow source correction is justified directly by FHIR-45047.

commits.author: Josh Mandel
commits.subject: FHIR-27752: Allow multiple related action data references
commits.summary: Corrected the current PlanDefinition action data-flow model so action.input.relatedData and action.output.relatedData can repeat, matching the final FHIR-27752 resolution.

triage.reviewer_summary: Jira-backed missed application: FHIR-27752 required PlanDefinition action input/output related data references to be repeatable, but the current PlanDefinition StructureDefinition still constrained both relatedData elements to one. This commit updates only those authoritative PlanDefinition cardinalities.
triage.category_rationale: FHIR-27752 was Published/Persuasive with Modification and specifically rejected adding DataRequirement.name in favor of complex PlanDefinition.action.input and PlanDefinition.action.output structures with title, requirement, repeatable relatedRequirementId-style references, and an invariant requiring either a requirement or related references but not both. The prior source application added the structures, relatedData elements, and xor constraints, but left PlanDefinition.action.input.relatedData and PlanDefinition.action.output.relatedData at max 1 instead of the resolved 0..* cardinality. Because source/plandefinition/structuredefinition-PlanDefinition.xml is the editor-owned StructureDefinition source for PlanDefinition, those stale max values affect generated conformance resources, rendered element tables, and validation behavior. Changing only those two max values to * is required to complete the accepted PlanDefinition model, not optional cleanup or generated collateral.
triage.fhir_spec_impact: The changed file is the authoritative PlanDefinition StructureDefinition source. The stale max 1 cardinalities incorrectly limited current PlanDefinition conformance and rendered cardinality tables to a single related input/output data reference where the accepted model permits multiple references.
triage.recommended_reviewer_action: Keep this as the Jira-backed PlanDefinition source fix for FHIR-27752. Do not broaden the change to RequestOrchestration or other action models without a separate tracker or work group decision.

jira_evidence.explanation: The resolution specifically required complex PlanDefinition.action.input and PlanDefinition.action.output structures with relatedRequirementId 0..* id references and an exclusive-or invariant. The current element name is relatedData, but the accepted repeatable cardinality requirement maps directly to the two relatedData elements changed here.

This later technical correction explains why the current PlanDefinition.action.input.relatedData type is string rather than id. It supports preserving the existing type while correcting only the missed cardinality.

This later RequestGroup/RequestOrchestration issue copied PlanDefinition-like definitional action aspects into another resource family, but it does not justify changing those other surfaces as part of this PlanDefinition-only correction.

caveats: The commit touches only source/plandefinition/structuredefinition-PlanDefinition.xml and contains no generated, derived, SVG, or editor-avoided files.
Equivalent cardinality questions for RequestOrchestration or other action models should be handled separately.

commits.author: Josh Mandel
commits.subject: FHIR-24827: Clarify Coverage boundaries
commits.summary: Updated the active Coverage Boundaries and Relationships section so its InsurancePlan row reflects the current InsurancePlan/InsuranceProduct split and no longer contains an unresolved TODO.

triage.reviewer_summary: Jira-backed missed application: keep this Coverage narrative fix, with attribution noting that FHIR-24827 is the direct split-specific decision and FHIR-17950 explains why the Coverage boundaries section exists. The current Coverage boundaries row still carried pre-split InsurancePlan wording and a visible TODO about InsuranceProduct even though FHIR-24827 resolved that Coverage.insurancePlan continues to reference the new InsurancePlan.
triage.category_rationale: FHIR-17950 required Coverage to have a Boundaries and Relationships section distinguishing Coverage from Contract and InsurancePlan. FHIR-24827 then made a concrete model decision: rename the old InsurancePlan concept to InsuranceProduct, move the plan backbone into a new InsurancePlan resource, make InsurancePlan.product reference InsuranceProduct, and keep Coverage.insurancePlan referring to InsurancePlan. The missed application is in source/coverage/coverage-introduction.xml, where the active Coverage boundaries table still described InsurancePlan with old product/offering wording and retained a reader-visible TODO asking whether InsuranceProduct should be referenced instead. That narrative conflicts with the resolved Coverage/InsurancePlan/InsuranceProduct relationship and is rendered as current Coverage guidance. The proposed edit is required to complete the application because it answers the Jira-resolved reference question, identifies InsuranceProduct only through InsurancePlan.product, and describes Coverage as identifying the plan for a beneficiary or subscriber rather than defining the reusable offering.
triage.fhir_spec_impact: source/coverage/coverage-introduction.xml is editor-owned narrative for the active Coverage resource page. This change affects rendered reader guidance by removing an unresolved TODO and replacing stale InsurancePlan text with wording aligned to the current Coverage.insurancePlan target and the current InsurancePlan.product relationship to InsuranceProduct.
triage.recommended_reviewer_action: Keep the source edit as a Jira-backed fix, but cite FHIR-24827 as the direct reason for the split-specific wording and FHIR-17950 as the source of the Coverage boundaries section.

jira_evidence.explanation: This Published/Persuasive Coverage issue requested a Boundaries and Relationships section distinguishing Coverage from Contract and InsurancePlan. It justifies the Coverage narrative surface, but it does not by itself require the later InsurancePlan/InsuranceProduct split wording.

This Applied/Persuasive resolution split the old InsurancePlan model into InsuranceProduct plus a new InsurancePlan, required InsurancePlan.product to reference InsuranceProduct, and explicitly stated that Coverage.insurancePlan will refer to InsurancePlan. That decision makes the old Coverage boundaries wording and the direct-InsuranceProduct TODO stale.

Later InsurancePlan boundary updates reportedly use the same model, describing Coverage as linking InsurancePlan to a beneficiary or subscriber. This supports the replacement wording but is not needed as the primary justification.

Later InsuranceProduct boundary updates reportedly mirror the same InsuranceProduct/InsurancePlan/Coverage relationship. This is supporting consistency evidence, not the direct required decision for this Coverage row.

caveats: The shown issue key is relevant to the existence and ownership of the Coverage boundaries section, but the exact stale wording is better attributed to the later InsurancePlan/InsuranceProduct split decision.
No generated, derived, layout-only, or hard-avoid files are changed.

The mapping-exception file is a checked-in source surface for the Appointment-to-Request pattern comparison; its hunk removes the same stale CodeableReference wording from the Request.note exception text rather than introducing a separate policy change.
triage.recommended_reviewer_action: Keep the commit as a Jira-backed source fix for FHIR-27849, with FHIR-19521 and FHIR-31523 as supporting context that Appointment.note and Appointment.patientInstruction are distinct approved changes.

jira_evidence.explanation: Resolved Published/Persuasive with Modification for R5 to change Appointment.patientInstruction from string 0..1 to CodeableReference(DocumentReference, Binary, Communication) 0..*, with examples for concept text, coded concept, and document/reference forms. Marked duplicate because multiple Appointment comments were handled by FHIR-27849 for patientInstruction and FHIR-19521 for note, reinforcing that the two approved changes are distinct.

commits.author: Josh Mandel
commits.subject: FHIR-44865: Restore STU marker for validate graph parameter
commits.summary: Restored the STU marker and explicit optional-support wording for Resource.$validate's graph parameter.

triage.reviewer_summary: Jira-backed missed application: FHIR-44865 required the Resource.$validate graph parameter to be added as an STU, optional-to-support parameter.
