commits.summary: Completed the published EpisodeOfCare clarification by removing stale Scope and Usage wording that implied every involved organization must have its own EpisodeOfCare instance.

triage.reviewer_summary: Jira-backed missed application: FHIR-20612 approved relaxing EpisodeOfCare wording so separate organization-specific EpisodeOfCare instances are not mandatory, but the active Scope and Usage narrative still stated that each organization will have its own instance. This commit updates that reader-visible narrative to align with the approved managingOrganization clarification.
triage.category_rationale: FHIR-20612 was Published as Persuasive with Modification and specifically required EpisodeOfCare.managingOrganization content to clarify that it represents the primary/overall organization responsible for care coordination while care may be provided by care teams from different organizations and other organizations may have their own EpisodeOfCare instances. The prior application updated the managingOrganization short, definition, and comment in the StructureDefinition, but missed the Scope and Usage paragraph in the active EpisodeOfCare introduction that still made separate instances sound mandatory for every involved organization. That paragraph is rendered resource guidance and directly conflicted with the approved clarification. Replacing the absolute wording with primary managing organization, multi-organization care-team, and optional separate-instance language is required to complete the approved clarification rather than optional cleanup.
triage.fhir_spec_impact: The changed file is active, editor-owned EpisodeOfCare narrative, so the stale paragraph affects rendered specification guidance for the current resource. The change does not alter conformance cardinality or resource structure, but it removes reader-visible text that contradicted the updated EpisodeOfCare.managingOrganization definition/comment.
triage.recommended_reviewer_action: Keep this as a Jira-backed source fix for FHIR-20612. Do not use this commit to decide broader cross-organization EpisodeOfCare modeling questions or the separate careTeam terminology correction.

jira_evidence.explanation: The Published Persuasive with Modification resolution required EpisodeOfCare.managingOrganization content to describe the overall responsible organization while allowing care teams from different organizations and only optional separate EpisodeOfCare instances for other organizations; the old Scope and Usage paragraph still used absolute each-organization wording.
A later issue is reported to address the historical EpisodeOfCare.team versus EpisodeOfCare.careTeam wording, but that separate correction is not needed to justify this narrative relaxation.
A later submitted issue concerns broader cross-organization EpisodeOfCare clarification; it shows related modeling questions remain open and should not be resolved by this narrow FHIR-20612 edit.

caveats: The fix is limited to the active narrative paragraph and should not be read as changing EpisodeOfCare.managingOrganization cardinality.
If careTeam path terminology is stale elsewhere, handle that under the later dedicated issue rather than broadening this commit.

commits.author: Josh Mandel
commits.subject: FHIR-20972: Correct Account balance source
commits.summary: Fixed remaining Account balance source inconsistencies from the published FHIR-20972 change.

triage.reviewer_summary: Jira-backed missed application: FHIR-20972 accepted reintroducing Account.balance with aggregate, term, estimate, amount, and calculatedAt, but the active Account source still had stale narrative, a wrong calculatedAt ElementDefinition path, and an incorrect balance-term CodeSystem value-set link. This commit is appropriate to keep as the missing source correction for the accepted Account.balance change.
triage.category_rationale: FHIR-20972 was Published/Persuasive with Modification for R5 and concretely required Account.balance 0..* with aggregate, term, estimate, amount, and calculatedAt. The prior application added that structure but missed three active source consequences: Account.balance.calculatedAt still declared its path as Account.calculatedAt, the Account introduction still told readers that direct balance representation was only future work, and the AccountBalanceTerm CodeSystem pointed to account-payment-terms instead of the balance-term value set used by Account.balance.term. These surfaces affect authoritative conformance and rendered terminology/narrative output, not just source-tree consistency. The edits are necessary to complete the accepted balance application because they make the child path match the approved backbone element, remove narrative that contradicts the approved balance property, and associate the balance-term code system with the intended value set.
triage.fhir_spec_impact: The StructureDefinition path correction affects the generated Account conformance resource for Account.balance.calculatedAt. The introduction text is rendered Account guidance, and the CodeSystem.valueSet correction affects terminology metadata for the Account balance term codes used by Account.balance.term.
triage.recommended_reviewer_action: Keep the commit as the FHIR-20972 missed source application. Treat later questions about aggregate wording or coverage-specific balance attribution as separate Account.balance work under their own resolved Jira decisions.

jira_evidence.explanation: The Published/Persuasive with Modification resolution explicitly required Account.balance 0..* with aggregate, term, estimate, amount, and calculatedAt. That requires calculatedAt to be a child of Account.balance, current Account guidance not to say direct balance representation is only future work, and the balance-term terminology metadata to reference the balance-term value set used for Account.balance.term.

caveats: The reviewed commit changes only Account introduction, CodeSystem, and StructureDefinition XML source; it does not include the SVG hunk mentioned in some surrounding notes.

commits.summary: Corrected the MedicinalProductDefinition.crossReference.type binding description so it describes product cross-reference relationships rather than unrelated extra measures.

triage.reviewer_summary: Jira-backed missed application: FHIR-25057 approved remodeling MedicinalProductDefinition.crossReference so it has a relationship type, but the current binding description for that type still described unrelated extra-measure semantics. The one-line StructureDefinition edit aligns the active conformance/rendered binding text with the approved cross-reference relationship element.
triage.category_rationale: FHIR-25057 was a Published/Persuasive BRR decision for R5 requiring MedicinalProductDefinition.crossReference to be a backbone element with a referenced product and MedicinalProductDefinition.crossReference.type representing the relationship between products. The backbone/product/type structure is present, but the authoritative binding description on crossReference.type still said "Extra measures defined for a Medicinal Product, such as heightened reporting requirements," which is the missed application because it contradicts the required relationship-type semantics and the ProductCrossReferenceType terminology. StructureDefinition binding descriptions feed the generated conformance resource and rendered element/binding content for an active resource, so the stale text affects current specification meaning for implementers. Replacing that description with relationship-to-another-product wording is required to complete the approved relationship-type application, not optional cleanup or generated collateral.
triage.fhir_spec_impact: The changed file is the authoritative StructureDefinition for an active resource. Its binding description is part of current conformance/rendered binding information for MedicinalProductDefinition.crossReference.type; without this edit, the spec would describe the product cross-reference relationship code as if it were about extra measures such as heightened reporting requirements.
triage.recommended_reviewer_action: Keep this as a Jira-backed fix to the authoritative StructureDefinition. Do not infer additional crossReference datatype or cardinality changes from this issue; those should remain tied to FHIR-26570 or a new BRR decision.

jira_evidence.explanation: The Published/Persuasive BRR request explicitly required MedicinalProductDefinition.crossReference to be remodeled so it can carry a product and a separate crossReference.type for the relationship between medicinal products. The stale binding description contradicted that approved role for the type element.

This later Published/Persuasive BRR issue changed crossReference.product to CodeableReference(MedicinalProductDefinition). It explains the current product datatype but does not replace FHIR-25057 as the basis for correcting the relationship-type binding text.

caveats: The current structure already reflects the backbone element and later CodeableReference refinement; this judgment is limited to the stale binding description for crossReference.type.

commits.author: Josh Mandel

The current missed surface was source/activitydefinition/operationdefinition-ActivityDefinition-apply.xml: the parameter had already been renamed to subject 1..*, but its documentation still said supplied subjects resolve as the subject of the PlanDefinition. That OperationDefinition source is the active conformance and operation-documentation source for ActivityDefinition/$apply, so the stale resource name gives the wrong target context in current operation text. triage.recommended_reviewer_action: Keep this as a narrow Jira-backed correction to the active ActivityDefinition/$apply OperationDefinition documentation.

This later issue discussed PlanDefinition/$apply and ActivityDefinition/$apply parameters as expression context variables. It supports the continued relevance of the $apply subject context but does not supersede or narrow the FHIR-18196 subject-resolution requirement.

commits.author: Josh Mandel
commits.subject: FHIR-45470: Clarify Specimen collector organization support
commits.summary: Clarified Specimen.collection.collector wording so the current source no longer describes an Organization-capable collector reference as person-only.

triage.reviewer_summary: Jira-backed missed application: FHIR-45470 approved direct Organization support for Specimen.collection.collector, but the authoritative element definition still described the collector as only a person. Keep this StructureDefinition wording update so the rendered definition and conformance resource match the approved collector target set.
triage.category_rationale: FHIR-45470 was resolved to add direct Organization support to Specimen.collection.collector, specifically a Reference to Organization with cardinality 0..1, so the element must describe an organization as a valid collector rather than only a person or an indirect PractitionerRole.organization path. The structural application added Organization to the targetProfile list and kept max 1, but source/specimen/structuredefinition-Specimen.xml still defined the element as "Person who collected the specimen.", directly conflicting with the approved Organization-capable collector semantics. ElementDefinition.definition in the Specimen StructureDefinition is authoritative source for rendered element definitions and distributed conformance content, so the stale person-only text affects current specification correctness. Changing the definition to "Individual or organization that collected the specimen." is required to complete the approved application, not optional consistency cleanup, and the commit only changes the editor-owned authoritative XML surface.
triage.fhir_spec_impact: source/specimen/structuredefinition-Specimen.xml is the authoritative Specimen StructureDefinition input. Its ElementDefinition.definition is rendered in the element definitions and carried in conformance output, so the previous person-only wording would mislead readers and implementers even though the targetProfile list already allows Organization.
triage.recommended_reviewer_action: Keep the StructureDefinition definition update as the Jira-backed completion of FHIR-45470's direct Organization collector support.

jira_evidence.explanation: The Applied OO resolution says to add Organization to Specimen.collection.collector, reference to Organization, cardinality 0..1. That directly requires the collector element to be described as Organization-capable; leaving the definition as person-only was an incomplete application after the targetProfile change.

This earlier Published issue broadened Specimen.collection.collector beyond a practitioner-only/person-only model for patient-collected specimens. It supports generic actor wording but is not the primary decision requiring this Organization-specific correction.

This later Specimen issue concerns an invariant around collector versus collection procedure performer. It does not justify this wording change, but it does not conflict with the FHIR-45470 collector Organization decision.

caveats: The reviewed commit changes only source/specimen/structuredefinition-Specimen.xml; no SVG, generated, or other hard-avoid file is part of this commit.

commits.author: Josh Mandel

triage.recommended_reviewer_action: Keep this as a Jira-backed source fix for FHIR-14833. Review the wording as the current application of the published Pharmacy decision, with FHIR-37372 retained only as supporting context for the separate usage-period plus last-administration guidance.

jira_evidence.explanation: The published Pharmacy resolution says dateTime supports year-only, year/month, and exact-date precision, says fuzzier values should be conveyed as text, and specifically directs that guidance to be added to MedicationStatement effectiveTime. That directly requires the partial-date guidance restored in MedicationStatement.effective[x].

This later published issue required comments on MedicationStatement.effective[x] explaining that a usage period and distinct last administration date/time should be represented with two MedicationStatement resources. The proposed text preserves that later guidance while adding back the older FHIR-14833 partial-date clarification.

caveats: The original application was to an older MedicationStatement source surface; the active StructureDefinition wording no longer carried the required partial-date guidance after later refactoring and effective[x] comment edits.

triage.reviewer_summary: Jira-backed missed application with mixed attribution: FHIR-40335 and FHIR-54036 explain why this core Observation notes paragraph exists, while FHIR-40384 is the decision that replaced the abandoned observation-recording extension with the published human-transcribed extension. The commit updates reader-visible Observation guidance to point to the actual extension and describe its approved semantics.
triage.category_rationale: FHIR-40384 resolved to add the Extension Pack Observation extension named human-transcribed, 0..1 boolean, for device data that was displayed, printed, or otherwise rendered for human consumption and then entered into the record; its history also records that the earlier observation-recording extension proposal was reopened and replaced. The missed application is that source/observation/observation-notes.xml still referred to the reverted observation-recording extension and still described recording the person or device that made versus entered the observation. That notes file is rendered as Observation narrative guidance, so the current spec would direct readers to a non-final extension name and stale recorder-identity semantics. The proposed edit is required to complete the application because it replaces exactly those stale reader-facing references with the published extension link and narrowed human-transcription wording, without touching generated collateral or unrelated cleanup.
triage.fhir_spec_impact: The changed file is current Observation narrative source and affects rendered guidance on the Observation page. Leaving the old wording would tell readers to use an extension name and recorder semantics that were superseded by the published boolean human-transcribed extension; this is a rendered-spec correctness issue rather than a generated-file or repository-hygiene cleanup.
triage.recommended_reviewer_action: Keep the source fix, but cite FHIR-40384 as the direct extension decision and FHIR-40335/FHIR-54036 as the core-text history explaining where the stale reference survived.

jira_evidence.explanation: Resolved Persuasive with Modification for FHIR-extensions to add the Observation human-transcribed extension, cardinality 0..1, type Boolean, with displayed/printed/rendered then human-entered semantics. Its comments show the previous observation-recording extension proposal with recorded and recorder subelements was reopened and replaced, so current core guidance should not continue to name or describe that abandoned extension.

Resolved Persuasive with Modification for FHIR-core to add Observation notes guidance about subject, focus, device, and an observation-recording extension. It explains why the core narrative surface exists and why it needs to stay aligned with the final extension decision, but the literal draft extension name was superseded by FHIR-40384.

Resolved Persuasive to move the recorder-related paragraph into a new Performer of an Observation section while preserving the observation-recording wording. It supports the current placement of the paragraph but does not supersede the final extension name and semantics from FHIR-40384.

triage.tooling_recommendation: Consider a link/reference check for narrative mentions of reverted or unpublished extension names, especially when an Extension Pack decision renames or narrows an extension referenced from core narrative.
caveats: The shown issue key is only partially responsible: FHIR-40335 introduced the core guidance family, while FHIR-40384 is the stronger attribution for replacing observation-recording with human-transcribed.
The commit touches only source/observation/observation-notes.xml; there are no generated, SVG, or other editor-avoided files to omit.

triage.reviewer_summary: Jira-backed missed application: FHIR-38853 explicitly required the QuestionnaireResponse.item group-nesting sentence to name item.item versus item.answer.item and required Questionnaire to point readers to the moved QuestionnaireResponse linkage diagram. This commit applies those remaining corrections in active, editor-owned specification source.
triage.category_rationale: FHIR-38853 was published as Persuasive with Modification and concretely required moving the linkage diagram to QuestionnaireResponse, updating the Questionnaire linkIds section to reference that QuestionnaireResponse section, and changing the sentence "Groups cannot have answers and therefore must nest directly within item" to say that contained group items are nested as item.item, not item.answer.item. The current source still missed that application: source/questionnaire/questionnaire-notes.xml linked the diagram back to questionnaire.html#link and described a local diagram on the right, while source/questionnaireresponse/structuredefinition-QuestionnaireResponse.xml retained the older indirect QuestionnaireResponse.item comment. The Questionnaire notes are rendered resource narrative and the QuestionnaireResponse StructureDefinition comment is authoritative conformance source, so the stale link/location text and missing explicit nesting rule affect current reader-visible guidance and generated element commentary. The edit is required to complete the published decision because it changes exactly the unresolved link text and exact group-nesting sentence named by the Jira, with no generated, diagram-only, or unrelated collateral files.
triage.fhir_spec_impact: source/questionnaire/questionnaire-notes.xml supplies rendered Questionnaire narrative guidance for linkIds and the QuestionnaireResponse linkage diagram reference. source/questionnaireresponse/structuredefinition-QuestionnaireResponse.xml supplies the authoritative QuestionnaireResponse.item comment used in generated definitions/conformance presentation, so the wording change affects current specification guidance about when nested content belongs under item.item versus item.answer.item.
triage.recommended_reviewer_action: Keep this as a Jira-backed source fix for FHIR-38853; the whole commit is within editor-owned source and no subset needs to be dropped.

jira_evidence.explanation: The published Persuasive with Modification resolution specifically required moving the linkage diagram to QuestionnaireResponse, updating Questionnaire to reference that section, and changing the QuestionnaireResponse.item group sentence to say contained items are nested as item.item, not item.answer.item.

This earlier published clarification introduced the group-versus-question nesting sentence that FHIR-38853 later refined; it supports the model distinction but is not the direct source of the exact remaining edit.

This published Not Persuasive with Modification resolution retained QuestionnaireResponse.item.answer.item and called for clearer guidance on when item.item and item.answer.item are used, supporting the same clarification direction.

This published clarification surfaced nested-question guidance in QuestionnaireResponse documentation and supports the current wording direction without replacing FHIR-38853 as the direct justification.

jira_evidence.explanation: The Jira description explicitly requested BodyStructure.includedStructure.spatialReference as 0..* Reference(ImagingSelection) with an invariant limiting use with bodyLandmarkOrientation. commits.author: Josh Mandel
commits.subject: FHIR-7319: Clarify diagnosis sequence identifiers
commits.summary: Clarified that Claim-family diagnosis.sequence values are reference identifiers, not primary/secondary diagnosis ordering.

triage.reviewer_summary: Jira-backed missed application: FHIR-7319 resolved that Claim diagnosis descriptions should remove diagnosis-order semantics because diagnosis.type identifies primary, secondary, admitting, discharge, and similar roles. triage.category_rationale: FHIR-7319 was Published/Persuasive and its final application comment specifically required diagnosis descriptions to remove the concept of diagnosis order because diagnosis.type now identifies the role of each diagnosis and the list is simply referenceable. The missed application is that the authoritative current StructureDefinition XML for Claim.diagnosis.sequence, and the copied parallel ExplanationOfBenefit.diagnosis.sequence text, still said diagnoses are presented in importance order and that sequence is necessary to maintain that order. These comments and requirements are emitted from active resource definitions into rendered element tables and generated conformance resources, so the stale wording creates current specification semantics contrary to the resolved rule. The edit is required to complete the resolved application because it removes only the ordering/ranking claim and leaves the valid reference-linking purpose of sequence intact; it is not generated collateral or optional cleanup.
triage.fhir_spec_impact: The changed files are editor-owned StructureDefinition XML inputs for active Claim and ExplanationOfBenefit resources. Their element comments and requirements affect current rendered definitions and generated conformance artifacts; before this edit, those surfaces told implementers that diagnosis.sequence conveyed primary/secondary-style ranking even though diagnosis.type carries those roles.
triage.recommended_reviewer_action: Keep the commit as a Jira-backed source fix. It touches only authoritative resource definitions, so downstream generated material should be regenerated normally.

jira_evidence.explanation: The issue asked how Claim diagnosis ordering works and whether the first diagnosis should be primary. The final application comment resolved that diagnosis.type identifies admitting, discharge, primary, secondary, and similar roles, and that descriptions should remove the concept of diagnosis order; that directly requires removing the order-maintenance language from Claim.diagnosis.sequence and supports applying the same correction to the active parallel ExplanationOfBenefit diagnosis sequence wording.

caveats: FHIR-7319 is recorded against Claim; the ExplanationOfBenefit hunk is included because it is an active FM StructureDefinition with the same copied diagnosis-order assertion and the same diagnosis.type role mechanism, not because it is generated or diagram collateral.
No hard-avoid SVG, generated model-definition, or derived summary file is part of this commit.

commits.author: Josh Mandel
commits.subject: FHIR-39512: Align Transport with event semantics
commits.summary: Aligned remaining Transport source with the Applied decision that Transport is an Event resource, not a Request resource.

triage.reviewer_summary: Real fix needing subset handling. FHIR-39512 directly supports correcting Transport's authoritative definition and narrative so Transport is described as an event resource, but the whole commit also deletes orphaned TransportIntent terminology files whose current publication/spec impact is not established.
triage.category_rationale: FHIR-39512 was Applied as Persuasive with Modification and specifically required Transport to be treated as an Event resource rather than a Request resource, including removing request-specific elements such as intent and priority and narrowing basedOn to approved authorizing request/Task targets. The current Transport.basedOn definition and Transport introduction still contained request-oriented prose, including a basedOn definition that referred to a request resource such as ServiceRequest or Transport and narrative saying Transport could be used in the request of a transport event and for request/fulfillment. Those editor-owned surfaces feed generated element definitions/conformance output and rendered Transport narrative, so correcting those hunks is required to complete the Jira decision. However, the commit also deletes the TransportIntent CodeSystem and ValueSet and synchronizes a mapping-exception text file; those changes are consistent with the event-only direction, but the available evidence proves only that the terminology is now unreferenced by active Transport source, not that the orphaned files are currently published or otherwise affecting rendered/conformance correctness. Because not every changed file is proven necessary for current spec correctness under the same Jira decision, this should be reviewed as a keep-subset change rather than a clean whole-commit Jira-backed missed application.
triage.fhir_spec_impact: The StructureDefinition edit affects the generated Transport.basedOn element definition and conformance resource, and the introduction edit affects reader-visible Transport narrative. The mapping-exception file appears to be comparison/workflow-pattern metadata and is reasonable to keep with the authoritative definition if reviewers use that source, but its independent current output impact was not proven. The change corrects reader-visible terminology-server guidance about how a server publishes support for additional external code systems; it does not touch generated files, examples, or diagram collateral.
triage.recommended_reviewer_action: Keep this as a Jira-backed source fix to the terminology-service narrative. Treat any broader decision about deprecating the old CapabilityStatement supported-system extension as separate extension-pack work.

jira_evidence.explanation: The Published/Persuasive resolution says server behavior capabilities will be documented in TerminologyCapabilities rather than CodeSystem, with documentation in CodeSystem and other appropriate places in the specification. The remaining active StructureDefinition description and root definition still described Person only as demographics independent of context, while the root comment said Person was a primary resource to point to for role actors; that omitted and partly contradicted the resolved rule. These fields feed the generated Person StructureDefinition and rendered resource/element documentation, so the stale wording affects current conformance and reader-facing content. Updating these exact structured text fields is required to finish applying the Jira decision, and FHIR-21241 further supports removing wording that implies Person can be the clinical or administrative actor target.
triage.fhir_spec_impact: source/person/structuredefinition-Person.xml is the active Person StructureDefinition source. Its description, root definition, and root comment are conformance and rendered documentation surfaces; before this edit, they were inconsistent with the current Person narrative and could mislead implementers about whether Person is a linkage resource rather than a role-specific actor reference target.
triage.recommended_reviewer_action: Keep as a Jira-backed source fix. Review the wording against the existing Person narrative and FHIR-21241 clarification, but there are no generated, layout-only, or editor-avoided files to split out.

jira_evidence.explanation: The issue resolved as Persuasive and agreed to update Person's definition/description to identify Person as a linking resource for shared demographics across Patient, Practitioner and RelatedPerson resources, and to state that Person instances are never directly referenced as actors. That directly requires the structured description, root definition, and actor-related comment to stop carrying generic or contradictory wording.

This later Published clarification required the Person actor-reference prohibition to be more obvious and says Person SHALL NOT be referenced by clinical or administrative resources. It supports replacing the old structured comment that implied Person was a primary actor-reference target.

This later DeviceRequest/VisionPrescription boundary issue supports leaving the DeviceRequest/VisionPrescription topic separate from the SupplyRequest removal. It does not require removing the remaining two-resource workflow question.

commits.summary: Removed stale current-resource-guide references to the retired DocumentManifest resource.

triage.reviewer_summary: Jira-backed missed application: FHIR-38865 removed DocumentManifest from core, but the current resource guide still presented it as a live Documents resource. This update removes the stale listing and aligns the guidance with DocumentReference plus List.
triage.category_rationale: FHIR-38865 was Published as persuasive with modification with the concrete OO motion to remove DocumentManifest. The main removal deleted source/documentmanifest and active registrations, but source/resourceguide.html still named DocumentManifest for grouped external documents and linked documentmanifest.html in the current resource table. That page is rendered reader-facing specification guidance, so the stale entry continued to advertise a removed resource as current content. Removing the row and replacing grouped-document guidance with List is required to complete the removal rather than optional cleanup, because it fixes the remaining current-page contradiction while leaving intentional history and compatibility references alone.
triage.fhir_spec_impact: source/resourceguide.html is a rendered narrative source page. Leaving DocumentManifest there would keep a removed resource visible in current Documents guidance and in a current resource table; this affects reader-visible specification content, not just repository hygiene.
triage.recommended_reviewer_action: Keep this as the Jira-backed source fix. Retain the resource guide update and leave intentional history, removed-resource, old-type, and compatibility references out of scope.

jira_evidence.explanation: The Published persuasive-with-modification resolution records an OO motion to remove DocumentManifest. That decision requires current core guidance not to list or link DocumentManifest as an active resource.
The earlier Published issue required an R5 retirement notice because IHE MHD had moved away from DocumentManifest toward List. It explains the retirement path but is not the final removal authority.
This Published issue moved XDS SubmissionSet guidance and examples from DocumentManifest to List, supporting List as the replacement wording for grouped document references.

caveats: The commit changes only source/resourceguide.html and does not include generated, derived, SVG, or other editor-avoided files.

The evidence supports removing current-page DocumentManifest references; residual mentions in history, removed-resource metadata, old-type mappings, and compatibility material should remain intentional unless separately reviewed.

The initial application created source/list/list-example-xds.xml as a List resource, but copied through xsi:schemaLocation="http://hl7.org/fhir ../../schema/documentmanifest.xsd", leaving the current List example internally inconsistent with the required migration. The changed file is the active List XDS example referenced by the List examples index, so the stale declaration affects the current XML example source used for the List specification/example surface and schema-aware validation or editing of that example. Changing that one declaration to ../../schema/list.xsd is necessary to complete the Jira-required migration of the example itself, not adjacent cleanup, because the example cannot coherently be the approved List replacement while declaring the retired DocumentManifest schema.
triage.fhir_spec_impact: The edit is in an editor-owned XML example under source/list, and list-List-examples.xml references it as List/example-xds. No generated or hard-avoid files are involved. The stale schemaLocation is not a FHIR data element, but it is part of the current XML example representation and can mislead schema-aware tooling or readers using the distributed/source XML example.
triage.recommended_reviewer_action: Keep the commit as a narrow Jira-backed correction to the active List XDS example.

jira_evidence.explanation: The Published/Persuasive resolution requested that List take over the XDS mappings and XDS SubmissionSet example from retired DocumentManifest. That directly requires the migrated example to be a coherent List example, including its XML schema declaration.
This Published/Persuasive with Modification issue removed DocumentManifest from core, reinforcing that an active List example should not continue to point to the retired DocumentManifest schema.

commits.author: Josh Mandel
commits.subject: FHIR-7805: Add Medication RXC text mapping
commits.summary: Added the missing RXC-2.2 Component Text entry to the active Medication.code HL7 v2 mapping, using Medication.code/code.text as the current-model target after Medication.name was removed.

triage.reviewer_summary: Jira-backed missed application: FHIR-7805 specifically approved adding RXC-2.2 Component Text to the Medication HL7 v2 text/name mapping. The current Medication StructureDefinition still lacked that text-component mapping on the active Medication.code surface after Medication.name was removed.
triage.category_rationale: FHIR-7805 was Published/Persuasive and its request text concretely required the Medication v2 name/text mapping to include RXC-2.2 Component Text alongside the existing RXO/RXE/RXD/RXG/RXA .2 text mappings. The current authoritative Medication StructureDefinition retained the paired v2 code-component mapping, including RXC-2.1 Component Code, but omitted the corresponding .2 text mapping that the Jira required; after FHIR-8553 removed Medication.name and moved textual medication description guidance to Medication.code, and FHIR-45876 reaffirmed that Medication.code.text can convey the medication name, Medication.code is the current source surface for that mapping. StructureDefinition mappings feed current rendered element mappings and conformance output, so the omission leaves the current spec without a Jira-required HL7 v2 text-component mapping. Adding the .2 text mapping to Medication.code is required to complete the approved mapping in the current model, not generated collateral or optional cleanup.
triage.fhir_spec_impact: The changed file is the editor-owned authoritative StructureDefinition source for Medication. Its v2 mapping content is exposed through current Medication conformance and rendered mapping surfaces, so this affects current spec mapping content rather than only repository hygiene.
triage.recommended_reviewer_action: Keep the source fix as a Jira-backed completion of the approved Medication v2 mapping change. No subset needs to be dropped because the commit changes only the authoritative Medication StructureDefinition mapping.

jira_evidence.explanation: The issue was Published/Persuasive and specifically requested adding RXC-2.2 Component Text to the Medication v2 name/text mapping. That is the exact missing mapping entry completed by this commit.

The companion Published/Persuasive issue required RXC-2.1 Component Code. That code-component mapping is already present in the current Medication.code v2 mapping, showing that the related code side was carried forward while the FHIR-7805 text side was not.

This later Published/Persuasive Medication issue removed Medication.name and updated Medication.code definition and guidance to cover textual medication descriptions. It supports placing the older name/text mapping on Medication.code in the current model rather than restoring Medication.name.

This later Medication decision confirms that Medication.code.text can convey the medication name. It supports the current-model target for the v2 text mapping but is not the primary source of the RXC-2.2 requirement.

caveats: The original FHIR-7805 wording referred to the old Medication.name/name-text mapping; later Medication decisions make Medication.code/code.text the current equivalent surface.

triage.category_rationale: FHIR-14421 specifically identified the Patient contact guidance example as wrong because it cited CarePlan.Participant, and the Jira comment states that CarePlan.participant had been replaced by the care-team participant path. triage.recommended_reviewer_action: Keep this narrow source fix as a direct application of FHIR-14421. No generated, derived, or editor-avoided files are involved.

jira_evidence.explanation: The issue specifically reported that the Patient.contact guidance cited CarePlan.Participant even though CarePlan had no Participant element, and the Jira comment identified the replacement through care-team participation. That is the same stale example fixed in the active Patient notes source.

This related clarification rewrote the same Patient.contact paragraph and appears to explain how the invalid CarePlan.participant wording reappeared, but it does not displace the narrower FHIR-14421 technical correction.

commits.author: Josh Mandel

The active source/codesystem/structuredefinition-CodeSystem.xml element for CodeSystem.count already includes the steward-defined definition, showing the Jira was only partially applied, but its comment still omitted the enumerated-code sentence required by the resolution. That XML is the authoritative conformance source for CodeSystem, so the omission affects generated StructureDefinition content and rendered element documentation. Adding the missing sentence to the CodeSystem.count comment is the direct necessary completion of the Jira application, not adjacent cleanup or generated collateral.
triage.fhir_spec_impact: The changed file is authoritative StructureDefinition XML for the active CodeSystem resource. The update changes current generated conformance content and rendered element documentation for CodeSystem.count; it is not limited to repository hygiene, an ignored source surface, or a layout-only artifact.
triage.recommended_reviewer_action: Keep this as a Jira-backed source fix for FHIR-16742; the patch applies the specific missing comment to the authoritative CodeSystem.count element.

jira_evidence.explanation: The Published resolution says to clarify that the system steward specifies the count for compositional code systems and to add a comment that usually the count is the total number of enumerated codes published as part of the code system. The patch adds exactly that missing comment sentence to CodeSystem.count.

caveats: This commit changes only source/codesystem/structuredefinition-CodeSystem.xml; no SVG or other editor-avoided generated-looking file is part of the actual patch being triaged.

commits.author: Josh Mandel
commits.subject: FHIR-7549: Clarify shared Dosage method guidance
commits.summary: Clarified the active shared Dosage.method definition/comment so current medication dosage instructions include the FHIR-7549 pre-coordination guidance.

triage.reviewer_summary: Jira-backed missed application: FHIR-7549 accepted concrete Dosage.method guidance explaining that method is often not populated because route or form may pre-coordinate it. The active shared Dosage datatype still carried the older terse note, so this commit completes that guidance on the current medication dosage source surface while preserving later FHIR-19913 examples.
triage.category_rationale: FHIR-7549 was Published/Persuasive with Modification and resolved to replace the old dosage.method pre-coordination note on MedicationAdministration, MedicationOrder, MedicationDispense, and MedicationStatement with explicit text saying the method is how medication is intended to be or was introduced, is most often not populated, and is often pre-coordinated in route and/or form. That wording was applied to then-current resource-specific dosage rows, but the later DosageInstruction-to-Dosage refactor created the active shared Dosage.method source with the older terse definition/comment. MedicationRequest, MedicationDispense, and MedicationStatement now use DosageDetails, whose simple and step.component entries are Dosage, and MedicationAdministration still has the clarified parallel element. Because source/datatypes/dosage.xml is authoritative datatype source, the stale row feeds current rendered datatype definitions and generated conformance text for those medication dosage instructions. Updating this row is required to complete the accepted guidance on the current source surface; it is not generated collateral or optional cleanup, and the commit touches only that editor-owned source file.
triage.fhir_spec_impact: source/datatypes/dosage.xml is an authoritative datatype spreadsheet. Its Dosage.method definition and comment are used for current rendered Dosage documentation and generated conformance artifacts, including medication dosage instructions reached through DosageDetails.simple and DosageDetails.step.component.
triage.recommended_reviewer_action: Keep as a Jira-backed source fix. Review it as the current shared Dosage/DosageDetails application of FHIR-7549, with FHIR-19913 explaining why the examples remain "inject, swallow, or chew" rather than the older FHIR-7549 examples.

jira_evidence.explanation: The resolution specifically required updating medication dosage.method definitions to explain that method is usually not populated when route or form pre-coordinate the method. The current shared Dosage datatype now carries the dosage-instruction method surface for MedicationRequest, MedicationDispense, and MedicationStatement through DosageDetails, so leaving its older short note was an incomplete application of that decision.

This later Published/Persuasive with Modification Pharmacy issue corrected the Dosage.method examples to "inject, swallow, or chew" and changed the binding basis. It does not supply the pre-coordination guidance, but it explains why this commit preserves the current examples while applying the older FHIR-7549 clarification.

caveats: The source-history mapping is important: a later DosageInstruction-to-Dosage change introduced the shared Dosage datatype, and current MedicationRequest, MedicationDispense, and MedicationStatement text says DosageDetails contains simple or structured Dosage.
MedicationAdministration.dosage.method already has the clarified FHIR-7549 guidance, so this commit appropriately leaves that resource-specific element alone.
The commit changes only source/datatypes/dosage.xml and does not include generated, derived, layout-only, or hard-avoid files.

commits.author: Josh Mandel
commits.subject: FHIR-12658: Clarify Account coverage priority ordering
commits.summary: Clarified Account.coverage.priority so the active Account source now carries the FHIR-12658 resolution's lower-values-first ordering rule.

triage.reviewer_summary: Jira-backed missed application: FHIR-12658 explicitly approved Account.coverage.priority as a positiveInt coordination-of-benefit priority where the lowest value applies first. The current Account StructureDefinition retained the priority element but omitted that approved ordering rule from the element definition.
triage.category_rationale: The FHIR-12658 resolution required a 0..* Account.coverage backbone with Account.coverage.coverage 1..1 Reference(Coverage) and Account.coverage.priority 0..1 positiveInt, using the coordination-of-benefit priority alias and lowest-value-first ordering. The active Account source already contains the backbone, Coverage reference, priority type, and alias, but its Account.coverage.priority definition only says it is the priority in the account context and does not state how numeric priority values are ordered. Because source/account/structuredefinition-Account.xml is the authoritative StructureDefinition input for the current Account resource, that omission affects generated element definitions and conformance-facing documentation. Adding the lower-values-first clause is required to complete the ordering semantics approved by FHIR-12658, not merely adjacent cleanup or generated collateral.
triage.fhir_spec_impact: The changed file is the editor-owned Account StructureDefinition source, so the definition text feeds current rendered element definitions and generated conformance resources. Without this edit, readers and implementers can see that Account.coverage.priority is an ordering priority but not the approved rule that lower numeric values are applied first.
triage.recommended_reviewer_action: Keep this as a Jira-backed source fix for FHIR-12658. The commit only changes the authoritative Account StructureDefinition source, so no generated-file or subset omission is needed.

jira_evidence.explanation: The Published, Persuasive with Modification resolution specifically required Account.coverage.priority as a 0..1 positiveInt coordination-of-benefit priority and stated that the lowest value applies first. That directly requires the Account.coverage.priority definition to convey the ordering rule.

This later Published PA issue renamed Account.period to Account.servicePeriod and explains why the period-name part of FHIR-12658 should not be reapplied here; it does not alter the Account.coverage.priority ordering requirement.

This later Applied FM clarification distinguishes use-case-independent Coverage.order from use-case-dependent Account.coverage.priority, supporting that Account.coverage.priority remains the correct account-context ordering surface.

caveats: FHIR-12658 also included an older period rename, but FHIR-14813 later renamed that element to Account.servicePeriod; this commit appropriately limits itself to the surviving Account.coverage.priority semantics.
No hard-avoid, generated, diagram-only, or derived files are changed.

commits.author: Josh Mandel
commits.subject: FHIR-38998: Clarify version label precedence
commits.summary: Clarified the active FHIR version-label documentation so readers know FHIR labels are not SemVer pre-release labels and SemVer precedence rules do not apply across label bases.

triage.reviewer_summary: Jira-backed missed application: FHIR-38998 specifically approved adding a note that FHIR version labels are not SemVer compliant and that SemVer precedence rules do not apply. This commit completes that note on the active versioning page without touching generated or collateral files.
triage.category_rationale: FHIR-38998 was Published/Persuasive and its resolution was concrete: add the requested note to the label section, namely that FHIR labels are not SemVer compliant, SemVer precedence rules cannot be applied to them, and labels are only sortable relative to labels with the same base. The existing source/versions.html text already had the same-label-base sorting sentence, but it still omitted the explicit SemVer non-compliance and precedence warning, so the prior application was incomplete. source/versions.html is the active Change Management and Versioning narrative page, so this omission affects current reader-facing versioning guidance. The proposed edit is required to complete the approved clarification because the remaining text did not tell readers not to treat FHIR labels as SemVer pre-release labels.
triage.fhir_spec_impact: source/versions.html is an editor-owned narrative source page for the rendered version-management documentation. The change updates reader-visible guidance about how FHIR version labels should be interpreted; it does not affect generated files, SVG/layout collateral, examples, or out-of-build source.
triage.recommended_reviewer_action: Keep this as the Jira-backed fix for FHIR-38998.

jira_evidence.explanation: The issue was Published/Persuasive for R5 and explicitly requested that the label section note labels are not SemVer compliant, that SemVer precedence rules cannot be applied, and that sorting is only defined for labels with the same base. The commit adds exactly that missing SemVer/precedence warning in source/versions.html.
This earlier issue established the major.minor.patch-label terminology and table that FHIR-38998 clarifies, but it is not the direct requirement for the SemVer label-precedence sentence.
This broader version-management cleanup involved the same page and related versioning policy, but it did not supersede or replace the label-specific clarification approved in FHIR-38998.

caveats: The commit changes only source/versions.html; there are no generated, derived, SVG, example-only, or hard-avoid files to omit.

commits.author: Josh Mandel
commits.subject: FHIR-38943: Complete Bundle profile registration
commits.summary: Completed the published Bundle profile application by registering the existing message-bundle profile in the Bundle-core IG and correcting batch-bundle to use the valid Bundle.type code batch.

triage.reviewer_summary: This is a Jira-backed missed application of the approved Bundle profile work. FHIR-38943 required standard informative Bundle-type profiles, but the current Bundle-core profile package omitted the existing message-bundle profile and the batch-bundle profile constrained Bundle.type to an invalid code.
triage.category_rationale: FHIR-38943 was Published as Persuasive with Modification for R5 and resolved to define standard informative profiles for Bundle types that manifest the rules for each Bundle use. The initial application added the Bundle profile StructureDefinitions and Bundle-core ImplementationGuide, but left message-bundle out of the Bundle-core IG and left batch-bundle fixing Bundle.type to `bundle`, which is not a Bundle.type code, rather than `batch`. Those files are current conformance/publication inputs: the IG controls which Bundle profiles are published in the Bundle-core package, and the StructureDefinition differential controls the batch profile constraint. Adding the missing message profile reference and correcting the batch type pattern are required to complete the approved Bundle profile application, not optional cleanup or generated collateral.
triage.fhir_spec_impact: Both changed files are editor-owned Bundle source used for current conformance publication. Without this update, the published Bundle profile package is incomplete and the batch Bundle profile contains an incorrect fixed Bundle.type value.
triage.recommended_reviewer_action: Keep this as the Jira-backed completion of FHIR-38943. Both hunks are authoritative source changes tied to the same approved Bundle profile decision; no generated or subset-only part needs to be dropped.

jira_evidence.explanation: The published resolution says to define standard informative profiles for Bundle types that manifest the rules for each profile type. That directly requires the Bundle-core package to include the existing message-bundle profile and requires each profile, including batch-bundle, to constrain Bundle.type to the valid code for that Bundle use.

caveats: This judgment covers the existing message-bundle registration and the invalid batch-bundle type code. Creating any additional collection-specific profile would need a separate work-group decision if the WG wants a type-fixing profile without additional collection-specific rules.

commits.author: Josh Mandel

Updating exactly those two references is required to complete the FHIR-46492 model refactor; FHIR-39033 explains why the Subscription filter resource discriminator remains, but it did not itself require this later path correction.

triage.recommended_reviewer_action: Keep the source change as a Jira-backed correction, but attribute it primarily to FHIR-46492. Treat FHIR-39033 as behavioral background for the retained resource discriminator rather than the direct basis for the path update.

The resolution retained the Subscription filter resource discriminator for multi-resource topics and required explanatory documentation. It supports the semantics of Subscription.filterBy.resource, but it did not require the later trigger-scoped canFilterBy path update.

The resolution renamed Subscription.filterBy.resourceType to Subscription.filterBy.resource. It explains the current element name used in the edited definitions, but not the canFilterBy cross-reference change.

triage.tooling_recommendation: Consider adding a consistency check for StructureDefinition prose references that name non-current element paths after model refactors.
caveats: The commit touches only source/subscription/structuredefinition-Subscription.xml, an editor-owned authoritative source file.
Any matching stale text in SVG diagram collateral should be regenerated or omitted rather than hand-edited.

The fix is therefore a real current-spec correction, but not a clean proof that the FHIR-38990 resolution itself was missed in core source.
triage.fhir_spec_impact: source/references.html is an active narrative page mapped by source/fhir.ini, so the malformed URL can appear in current rendered specification guidance and send readers to an unreachable host. The change does not alter conformance resources, examples, or validation behavior; it corrects reader-visible navigation from core text to an existing Extension Pack definition.
triage.recommended_reviewer_action: Keep the hyperlink correction as an editorial/current-page fix, preferably under a small link-fix issue, editorial rollup, or better attribution if one exists. jira_evidence.explanation: The Published/Persuasive resolution approved separating CanonicalResource.date from publication date and defining it as the date the artifact was last significantly changed. triage.recommended_reviewer_action: Keep the source change as a Jira-backed correction to the authoritative transaction response example.

jira_evidence.explanation: The Published/Persuasive R5 resolution says that when conditional create finds one match, the server returns 200 OK with headers and body populated as if a create had actually occurred. The request text explicitly covers batch and transaction responses, naming Location, ETag, Last-Modified, Bundle.entry.response properties, and returned resource behavior.

commits.author: Josh Mandel
commits.subject: FHIR-31900 + FHIR-34136: Clarify Task restriction period timing
commits.summary: Clarified Task.restriction.period so it no longer describes executionPeriod as requested timing, uses the actual ServiceRequest.occurrence[x] element name, and keeps the Task SVG tooltip spelling aligned.

triage.reviewer_summary: This is a Jira-backed missed application with mixed attribution: FHIR-31900 established Task.restriction.period as the fulfillment period within a referenced request, and FHIR-34136 later made the retained executionPeriod/deadline wording incorrect. The commit changes only the authoritative Task StructureDefinition, so it is appropriate to review as a spec-facing correction.
triage.category_rationale: FHIR-31900 specifically required Task.restriction.period to describe the time period for which fulfillment is sought within the referenced request authorization, with an example tied to ServiceRequest.occurrence[x]; FHIR-34136 then specifically added Task.requestedPeriod for desired completion timing and defined Task.executionPeriod as actual execution timing, distinct from restriction.period. The current Task.restriction.period definition and comment still misspelled ServiceRequest.occurrence[x], described executionPeriod as requested/initiation timing, and treated period.high as a task due date, so the accepted Task timing semantics were incompletely applied. Because these strings are element definition/comment content in source/task/structuredefinition-Task.xml, they feed the rendered Task definitions and generated StructureDefinition. The proposed edit is required to complete the accepted application because it corrects the request element reference and replaces the contradictory timing guidance with the approved requestedPeriod/executionPeriod distinction, rather than making optional cleanup or generated collateral changes.
triage.fhir_spec_impact: source/task/structuredefinition-Task.xml is the authoritative Task StructureDefinition. The changed definition and comment affect current rendered Task element definitions and generated conformance content by removing a misspelled ServiceRequest element reference and guidance that otherwise contradicts the current meanings of Task.requestedPeriod and Task.executionPeriod.
triage.recommended_reviewer_action: Keep the source change, with attribution to FHIR-31900 plus FHIR-34136 rather than FHIR-31900 alone.

jira_evidence.explanation: The resolution required Task.restriction.period to describe the period for which fulfillment is sought within the referenced request authorization and cited the request occurrence element. That supports correcting the ServiceRequest.occurrence[x] example and preserving restriction.period as authorization-scope guidance rather than a standalone task deadline.

The later resolution added Task.requestedPeriod for desired completion timing and defined Task.executionPeriod as actual execution timing, with requestedPeriod distinct from restriction.period. That is the direct reason the old Task.restriction.period comment about executionPeriod being requested/initiation timing and period.high being the due date must be updated.

This later Task.restriction resolution refined the restriction comment while preserving the same fulfillment-of-a-request limitation, supporting the narrowed interpretation without being the main timing fix.

caveats: The timing correction should cite FHIR-34136; FHIR-31900 alone explains why restriction.period exists and how it relates to request authorization, but its original usage note predates the current requestedPeriod/executionPeriod terminology.
The reviewed commit changes only source/task/structuredefinition-Task.xml; no SVG or other generated-looking collateral is part of this commit.

commits.author: Josh Mandel
commits.subject: FHIR-31986: Fix Bundle bdl-7 uniqueness invariant
commits.summary: Updated Bundle bdl-7 so duplicate fullUrls are checked only for entries with a resource, using fullUrl plus meta.versionId with a delimiter and preserving the later empty-versionId fallback.

triage.reviewer_summary: Jira-backed missed application: FHIR-31986 explicitly resolved to rewrite Bundle bdl-7 so entries with the same fullUrl are compared only when a resource is present and are distinguished by meta.versionId. The current Bundle StructureDefinition still carried the older history-bundle exception and ambiguous fullUrl/version concatenation, so this commit completes the resolved invariant update.
triage.category_rationale: FHIR-31986's published FHIR-I resolution required concrete bdl-7 source changes: replace the human text with the resource-present fullUrl/version rule and replace the expression with entry.where(fullUrl.exists() and resource.exists()).select(fullUrl&'|'&resource.meta.versionId).isDistinct(). The current authoritative Bundle StructureDefinition had not applied that requirement; it still exempted all history bundles and selected fullUrl plus version without the resource-present filter or delimiter, with only the later missing-version fallback from FHIR-39476 present. Because bdl-7 is the machine-readable Bundle invariant in StructureDefinition/Bundle, the stale expression affects generated conformance and validation semantics for current Bundle instances, including history deletes and batch HEAD entries versus resource-bearing duplicate fullUrls. The proposed edit is required to complete the FHIR-31986 application while preserving FHIR-39476's later iif(..., '') correction, rather than being optional consistency cleanup.
triage.fhir_spec_impact: source/bundle/structuredefinition-Bundle.xml is the authoritative Bundle StructureDefinition input. Updating bdl-7 changes the rendered constraint text and the generated machine-readable invariant used by validators and conformance consumers, narrowing the old whole-history exception to entries where resource is absent and avoiding false collisions from direct fullUrl/version concatenation.
triage.recommended_reviewer_action: Keep this as the FHIR-31986-backed Bundle invariant fix. Reviewers should verify the retained FHIR-39476 missing-version fallback is intentional, but no subset should be dropped.

jira_evidence.explanation: The published Not Persuasive with Modification resolution gives the exact replacement bdl-7 human text and FHIRPath expression: entries with the same fullUrl where resource is present must have different meta.versionId, using fullUrl plus a delimiter plus versionId. This directly requires the source update in StructureDefinition/Bundle.

This later published issue corrected bdl-7's handling of absent meta.versionId by adding an empty-string fallback. The reviewed commit appropriately preserves that later correction while applying the still-missing FHIR-31986 resource-present scope and delimiter.

This earlier issue introduced the broad history-bundle exception for deleted entries without resource bodies. FHIR-31986 narrowed that rationale to entries where resource is absent, so FHIR-18284 explains the stale source shape but does not supersede the later required rewrite.

This earlier bdl-7 correction added the fullUrl.exists() filter and is useful invariant history. It does not independently require the current commit, but it supports preserving that part of the expression.

caveats: The expression differs from the literal FHIR-31986 resolution by keeping FHIR-39476's later iif(..., '') fallback for absent meta.versionId; that is a preservation of a subsequent published correction, not a separate unsupported change.

commits.author: Josh Mandel
commits.subject: FHIR-31944: Clarify POST search parameter equivalence
commits.summary: Clarified the active HTTP search narrative so accepted POST URL and body parameters are treated as one parameter set, and unsupported POST URL parameters may be rejected or ignored with the self link reflecting actual processing.

triage.reviewer_summary: Jira-backed missed application: FHIR-31944 specifically required POST search guidance to say that accepted URL and body parameters are semantically equivalent, and that unsupported POST URL parameters may be rejected or ignored with the self link reflecting the parameters actually processed. This commit applies that missing rule in the active REST HTTP search narrative.
triage.category_rationale: FHIR-31944 was resolved to clarify POST search by stating that servers SHALL support body parameters, MAY support URL parameters, may restrict URL parameters and reject or ignore unsupported ones, SHALL treat parameters present in both URL and body as semantically equivalent, and SHALL express the self link with parameters in the URL. Before this change, source/http.html already showed POST body parameters and optional URL query parameters, but it still omitted the required equivalence rule and only described rejection of restricted URL parameters, leaving out the resolved ignore-with-self-link behavior. That page is the current rendered REST HTTP search guidance, so the omission affects reader-facing and conformance-facing behavior for POST search processing. The edit is required to complete the exact Jira resolution because it adds the two missing semantics in the active source section and does not touch generated, derived, or unrelated files.
triage.fhir_spec_impact: source/http.html is active narrative for REST search behavior. The changed text affects current rendered guidance and normative-style server behavior by explaining how POST search parameters split between URL and form body are combined, and how unsupported URL query parameters may be ignored while the self link reports the parameters actually used.
triage.recommended_reviewer_action: Keep as a Jira-backed fix for FHIR-31944. No subset should be dropped; the only changed file is the editor-owned HTTP page source.

jira_evidence.explanation: The Published/Persuasive with Modification resolution explicitly required POST search guidance for body-parameter support, optional URL parameters, URL-parameter restrictions with reject-or-ignore handling, semantic equivalence between URL and body parameters, and URL-form self links. The commit implements the remaining equivalence and ignore/self-link portions in source/http.html.
The companion POST search method issue explains the broader GET/POST support and 405 context, but it is not the direct basis for the URL/body equivalence wording applied here.

This later issue made explicit that POST search self links are always GET-style URLs. It supports the reference to self-link behavior, while the specific ignore-and-reflect-actual-processing rule comes from FHIR-31944.

This later POST search issue added additional POST search forms and examples, explaining why other parts of FHIR-31944 were already represented and why this commit is limited to the remaining semantic gap.
This later editorial refactor moved transport-protocol guidance to source/http.html, which is the current source surface where the FHIR-31944 equivalence and ignore behavior needed to appear.
