triage.reviewer_summary: Jira-backed missed application: FHIR-28307 explicitly approved moving the ElementDefinition.comment parenthetical rendering-source note out of the Definition text and into the Comment text. This commit applies that correction in the active ElementDefinition datatype source and fixes the requested note punctuation.
triage.category_rationale: FHIR-28307 was a Published/Persuasive FHIR-core technical correction whose resolution says to move the bracketed text in the ElementDefinition.comment definition down into the comment, and the issue request also called for the note-ending periods to be inside the parentheses. The current ElementDefinition datatype source still had the ElementDefinition.comment note in the Definition cell, so the approved correction remained incompletely applied. Because source/datatypes/elementdefinition.xml is the authoritative spreadsheet source for the ElementDefinition datatype, those Definition and Comment cell values feed the current rendered datatype documentation and generated conformance content. Moving the note to the Comment cell, while leaving the ElementDefinition.definition note in its Definition cell with corrected punctuation, is the direct change required to complete the approved correction rather than adjacent cleanup or generated collateral.
triage.fhir_spec_impact: The changed file is authoritative ElementDefinition datatype source, so the affected text appears in current rendered ElementDefinition documentation and generated StructureDefinition-derived content. Before this edit, ElementDefinition.comment's definition incorrectly contained a note claiming the reader-visible text was specified in ElementDefinition.comment; after this edit, the note is located in the Comment text as approved.
triage.recommended_reviewer_action: Keep as a Jira-backed source fix for FHIR-28307. The commit touches only the editor-owned ElementDefinition datatype source needed for the approved correction, so no subset should be dropped.

jira_evidence.explanation: Published/Persuasive FHIR-core technical correction. The description says the ElementDefinition.comment note should be moved down to the ElementDefinition.comment Comment text and that the note-ending periods should be inside the parentheses; the resolution confirms moving the bracketed text in the comment definition down into the comment.

Published earlier issue that introduced the parenthetical rendering-source notes in ElementDefinition text. It explains why the stale note existed but does not supersede the later FHIR-28307 correction.

Later applied issue concerns separate MustSupport guidance in profiling text. It does not justify this ElementDefinition cell move, but the related discussion confirms continuing confusion around ElementDefinition.definition versus ElementDefinition.comment.

caveats: FHIR-I minutes from 2020-12-07 record FHIR-28307 as 'Will fix as suggested' and a Technical Correction, corroborating the Jira resolution.
The commit does not include generated files, SVGs, example cleanup, or other editor-avoided collateral.

commits.author: Josh Mandel
commits.subject: FHIR-11341: Correct ServiceRequest status comment
commits.summary: Corrected the current ServiceRequest.status request-pattern comment so it uses the valid status term completed rather than the non-code typo competed, preserving the FHIR-11341 intent that status prose not name obsolete or invalid status values.

triage.reviewer_summary: Real ServiceRequest.status wording fix needing separate attribution. The current authoritative comment says an activated order may be "competed", which is not a RequestStatus code, but the cited Jira resolutions do not explicitly approve the one-word correction to "completed".
triage.category_rationale: FHIR-11341 required DiagnosticRequest.status to stop saying the requester sets status to "requested" and to use the request-pattern status comment; FHIR-12254 supplied that request-pattern wording. Those resolutions support the general status-comment lineage, but their approved wording itself contains "competed", so the exact "competed" to "completed" repair is a terminology-correctness fix inferred from the current RequestStatus CodeSystem rather than a concrete missed application of the Jira text. The current ServiceRequest.status comment is nevertheless wrong because it names a non-code word where the active status vocabulary has "completed".
triage.fhir_spec_impact: source/servicerequest/structuredefinition-ServiceRequest.xml is authoritative StructureDefinition source, so the comment affects rendered element definitions and distributed conformance content. source/servicerequest/servicerequest-request-mapping-exceptions.xml mirrors the same ServiceRequest-specific request-pattern text for the comparison/mapping exception surface; keeping it aligned is reasonable if the source wording fix is accepted.
triage.recommended_reviewer_action: Consider applying this as a small technical correction under a new or rollup Jira rather than treating it as fully covered by FHIR-11341. If accepted, keep both the ServiceRequest StructureDefinition comment and its request-pattern mapping-exception mirror in sync.

jira_evidence.explanation: This resolved that DiagnosticRequest.status should no longer say the requester sets status to "requested" and should use the request-pattern comment. It supports avoiding non-status terms in request status prose, but the resolution does not specifically require changing "competed" to "completed".

This supplied the shared _Request.status wording referenced by FHIR-11341, but the approved wording also says "competed". It therefore cannot establish that the current ServiceRequest source missed an approved "completed" wording.

This merged DiagnosticRequest and ProcedureRequest into the later request-resource lineage, explaining why ServiceRequest is the current successor surface for old DiagnosticRequest status guidance. It does not decide the "competed" versus "completed" wording.

This supports later cleanup from cancelled/suspended terminology to revoked/on-hold in current request status text. It explains the surrounding ServiceRequest.status wording but does not specifically require the completed typo fix.

triage.tooling_recommendation: A terminology-aware check for comments that mention near-miss or non-code status words such as "competed" could catch this class of conformance-source typo.
caveats: No hard-avoid SVG or generated library files are touched.

The change appears substantively correct because RequestStatus includes completed and not competed, but the explicit Jira resolution text is not enough to prove this as a missed application of FHIR-11341.

commits.author: Josh Mandel
commits.subject: FHIR-20521: Flag Observation component value for obs-7
commits.summary: Added the missing obs-7 ElementDefinition.condition tag to Observation.component.value[x].

triage.reviewer_summary: Jira-backed missed application: FHIR-20521 specifically identified Observation elements affected by obs-7, including Observation.component.value, that should carry ElementDefinition.condition metadata. The commit adds the one missing obs-7 condition tag to the authoritative Observation StructureDefinition source.
triage.category_rationale: FHIR-20521 was resolved Persuasive/Applied for R6 by OO after reporting that Observation.code, Observation.value, Observation.component.code, and Observation.component.value were not all flagged as affected by obs-7; the reporter clarified Observation.value was already flagged. Current Observation source already carried obs-7 on the other requested surfaces, but Observation.component.value[x] still had only obs-10 and therefore incompletely applied the requested condition coverage. Because source/observation/structuredefinition-Observation.xml is the editor-owned StructureDefinition input for Observation, this omission affects generated conformance metadata and rendered structure/invariant indicators for the current resource. Adding <condition value="obs-7"/> to Observation.component.value[x] is the remaining required source update for that Jira decision, not optional cleanup or generated collateral.
triage.fhir_spec_impact: The changed file is the authoritative Observation StructureDefinition XML. ElementDefinition.condition is emitted in the generated StructureDefinition and used by rendered element tables/invariant indicators, so the pre-change source omitted obs-7 metadata from Observation.component.value[x] even though the applied Jira decision said that element is affected by the invariant.
triage.recommended_reviewer_action: Keep this as the Jira-backed source fix for FHIR-20521. The commit only changes an editor-owned conformance source file, so no subset should be omitted or regenerated separately.

jira_evidence.explanation: The issue was resolved Persuasive/Applied for R6 by OO and specifically reported that Observation elements involved in obs-7, including Observation.component.value, were not all flagged with ElementDefinition.condition; the current source still lacked obs-7 on Observation.component.value[x].

The broader condition-consistency issue declined a general automated rule and asked for specific tracker items; source history under that cleanup explains why several Observation obs-7 condition tags were added while this FHIR-20521 surface remained incomplete.
The later no-change decision about the obs-7 expression supports leaving the invariant expression untouched; it does not replace FHIR-20521 as the basis for the missing condition metadata.

The separate obs-10 correction confirms the same element legitimately carries condition metadata for applicable invariants, but it concerns a different invariant and is not the justification for adding obs-7.

triage.tooling_recommendation: None.

commits.author: Josh Mandel
commits.subject: FHIR-20203 + FHIR-24869: Restore operation response output wording
commits.summary: Fixed a one-letter typo in the active Operations Framework response paragraph introduced when the Published FHIR-24869 zero-output response guidance was applied.

triage.reviewer_summary: Jira-backed missed application: this one-line edit restores the dropped leading letter in active Operations Framework response wording. FHIR-24869 explains the same response paragraph being edited, while FHIR-20203 is the clearest source for the exact approved phrase "one or more output parameters."
triage.category_rationale: FHIR-20203 resolved the operation execution text to say that a completed operation returns a Parameters resource containing "one or more output parameters," and FHIR-24869 later required augmenting operations.html#response for operations with zero out parameters while preserving the distinction between Parameters responses and omitted bodies. The current source still says "ne or more output parameters" in that active response paragraph, so the approved wording was not correctly preserved when the FHIR-24869 zero-output guidance and later related edits were applied. Because source/operations.html is an active Operations Framework narrative page, the typo is rendered as current specification text. Changing "ne" back to "one" is the minimal required source correction to complete the Jira application, not generated collateral, optional consistency cleanup, or a new policy change.
triage.fhir_spec_impact: source/operations.html is reader-visible narrative for operation responses. The change fixes current rendered specification text; it is editorial and restores the intended sentence without changing the conformance rule for Parameters wrapping, zero-output responses, or single Resource return values.
triage.recommended_reviewer_action: Keep the one-line source fix. Record the attribution nuance: FHIR-24869 is relevant because its application touched this response paragraph and introduced the typo, but FHIR-20203 directly supplies the restored "one or more output parameters" wording.

jira_evidence.explanation: The Published/Persuasive resolution gave concrete replacement operation text stating that the returned Parameters resource contains "one or more output parameters." The current "ne or more" text fails to preserve that approved wording.

The Published/Persuasive resolution required operations.html#response to describe zero-output operations, including appropriate success/error status codes and possible empty response bodies. Applying that guidance to the same response discussion left the sentence with a dropped leading letter, so completing the application requires restoring the readable one-or-more Parameters wording while leaving the zero-output guidance intact.
This later Published/Persuasive issue revised the same sentence for a single 0..1 Resource return value. It is compatible with restoring "one" and does not provide a reason to retain the typo.

caveats: This is a typo repair in active narrative, not a semantic change to operation response behavior.

commits.author: Josh Mandel
commits.subject: FHIR-28291: Restore Group characteristic-reference search
commits.summary: Restored Group-characteristic-reference to a reference SearchParameter so /Group?characteristic-reference=Organization/123 remains supported.

triage.reviewer_summary: Jira-backed missed application: FHIR-28291 approved a plain Group characteristic-reference search, but the current SearchParameter source had drifted into a composite parameter. This commit restores the authoritative Group search parameter to the reference semantics the Jira requested.
triage.category_rationale: FHIR-28291 was Published/Persuasive and specifically requested that /Group?characteristic-reference=Organization/123 return Groups with any characteristic whose value references Organization/123; the recorded FHIR-I decision was to add that suggested search parameter. The missed application is that source/group/bundle-Group-search-params.xml currently defines Group-characteristic-reference as a composite over Group.characteristic with code and reference components, which no longer represents the approved plain reference query. Because this bundle is the editor-owned source for the active Group SearchParameter resources, the type, expression, description, and component structure affect the rendered/conformance SearchParameter definition and server-facing search semantics. Restoring type=reference with expression Group.characteristic.value.ofType(Reference) and removing the composite components is required to complete the approved Jira behavior, not merely adjacent cleanup.
triage.fhir_spec_impact: The changed file is an authoritative conformance source bundle for the active Group resource. The stale composite definition changes the published SearchParameter type and expression/components, so it affects current conformance output and the advertised ability to use /Group?characteristic-reference=Organization/123 as a reference search rather than a composite value joined with '$'.
triage.recommended_reviewer_action: Keep this as a Jira-backed fix to the Group SearchParameter source. If the work group wants an additional code-plus-reference composite search, handle that separately under a distinct Jira and parameter design rather than replacing this reference search.

jira_evidence.explanation: The issue was Published/Persuasive for FHIR-core Group and asked for /Group?characteristic-reference=Organization/123 to match Groups whose characteristic value references that Organization. That concrete request requires a reference SearchParameter over Group.characteristic.value, not a composite parameter requiring separate code and reference components.

This later Applied issue concerned quantity/range search behavior and search-type wording; its resolution does not approve replacing the FHIR-28291 reference search with a composite. It therefore does not supersede or narrow the FHIR-28291 requirement.

caveats: The commit touches only source/group/bundle-Group-search-params.xml; no hard-avoid generated, derived, or layout-only files are included.
Later source history may explain where the drift was introduced, but the necessary reviewer decision here is directly supported by FHIR-28291.

commits.author: Josh Mandel
commits.subject: FHIR-13813: Align expansion identifier prose with optional cardinality
commits.summary: Aligned active ValueSet narrative with the already-applied 0..1 cardinality for ValueSet.expansion.identifier.
commits.stat:
source/valueset/valueset-introduction.xml |  2 +-
 source/valueset/valueset-notes.xml        | 11 ++++++-----
 2 files changed, 7 insertions(+), 6 deletions(-)

triage.reviewer_summary: Jira-backed missed application: FHIR-13813 made ValueSet.expansion.identifier optional, but active ValueSet prose still said every expansion has or SHALL have one. Keep this as a correction to reader-visible narrative that now matches the already-correct 0..1 conformance source.
triage.category_rationale: FHIR-13813 was Published/Persuasive and specifically resolved to change ValueSet.expansion.identifier cardinality to 0..1 because terminology servers are not required to persist expansions or generate identifiers for transient $expand results. The current StructureDefinition source already has min 0/max 1, but source/valueset/valueset-introduction.xml still said any expansion has ValueSet.expansion.identifier and source/valueset/valueset-notes.xml still said each expansion SHALL have a unique identifier. Those active narrative files are rendered ValueSet specification guidance, so the mandatory prose contradicted the current conformance resource and the Vocabulary WG decision. The edit is required to complete the cardinality change in the narrative, while preserving uniqueness requirements only when an identifier is present.
triage.fhir_spec_impact: The changed files are active ValueSet narrative source used for rendered specification text. Before the edit, readers saw mandatory expansion-identifier guidance that conflicted with ValueSet.expansion.identifier 0..1; the commit removes that contradiction without changing generated files, examples, or unrelated conformance definitions.
triage.recommended_reviewer_action: Keep as a Jira-backed correction to active ValueSet narrative. No subset omission is needed because the commit only touches editor-owned narrative source.

jira_evidence.explanation: The resolution says to change ValueSet.expansion.identifier cardinality to 0..1 as requested, based on the stated problem that terminology servers need not persist expansions or generate identifiers for transient expansion results. That decision requires removing active prose that still says every expansion has or SHALL have an identifier.
This earlier decision made expansion.identifier a uri and 1..1, explaining the origin of the mandatory identifier rule that FHIR-13813 later relaxed.

This later clarification adjusted the element short description to the current business-identifier wording, supporting preservation of the identifier concept while fixing only the stale optionality language.

commits.author: Josh Mandel
commits.subject: FHIR-28495: Correct If-None-Match update guidance
commits.summary: Corrected the core HTTP page so If-None-Match: * is documented for update-as-create with PUT [type]/[id], not as a search-based conditional update rule.

triage.reviewer_summary: Jira-backed missed application: FHIR-28495 specifically approved If-None-Match: * for PUT [type]/[id] update-as-create, but the HTTP page still documented the rule under search-based conditional update. This commit moves the rule, wildcard-only allowance, 412 failure behavior, and summary-table guidance to the rendered update-as-create surface.
triage.category_rationale: FHIR-28495 resolved to update the specification to support If-None-Match: * for PUT [type]/[id], allowing a client to create a resource with a client-specified id only when that id is not already present, and to document that servers may support only the wildcard variant for this use case. The missed application is that source/http.html still placed the If-None-Match discussion under conditional update and led with an ETag-specific W/"[ETag]" example, while the update interaction summary omitted If-None-Match. Because source/http.html is the rendered RESTful HTTP interaction page, this stale placement affected current implementer-facing behavior text and summary guidance. The proposed edit is necessary to complete the Jira application because it relocates the rule to Update as Create, states the 412 Precondition Failed behavior when the target resource exists, records the wildcard-only allowance, and removes the misleading conditional-update paragraph rather than making unrelated cleanup.
triage.fhir_spec_impact: source/http.html is an authoritative rendered HTTP interaction page. The change affects reader-visible REST guidance and the interaction summary table by documenting If-None-Match: * for update-as-create with PUT [type]/[id], instead of leaving readers with misleading conditional-update and ETag-specific guidance.
triage.recommended_reviewer_action: Keep this as the FHIR-28495-backed HTTP page fix. Do not broaden this commit to transaction Bundle ifNoneMatch behavior or CapabilityStatement discovery; those surfaces need their own scoped tracker or CapabilityStatement2 path.

jira_evidence.explanation: The Published, Persuasive with Modification resolution says to update the spec to support If-None-Match: * for PUT [type]/[id] and to document that servers can choose to support only the wildcard variant for this conditional PUT/update-as-create use case. That directly requires the source/http.html update-as-create prose and summary-table changes in this commit.
FHIR-42728 later addressed conditional interaction codes and Trial Use markers. It does not define the If-None-Match update-as-create rule and is not the basis for this source edit.

caveats: The discovery-mechanism portion of FHIR-28495 was later deferred to CapabilityStatement2 work, so this commit is appropriately limited to HTTP interaction prose and summary guidance.

triage.recommended_reviewer_action: Keep the source edit as the remaining Jira-backed documentation fix for FHIR-28491.

jira_evidence.explanation: The Published/Persuasive R5 request explicitly says to update Subscription.topic to a canonical reference and add documentation that clients needing the SubscriptionTopic can search SubscriptionTopic resources and/or attempt canonical resolution, with direct retrieval not always possible. This later Subscription documentation issue updated broader subscription text about subscription styles, but it did not replace or narrow the specific Subscription.topic lookup guidance required by FHIR-28491.

commits.author: Josh Mandel

triage.fhir_spec_impact: source/careplan/careplan-introduction.xml is active narrative source, so the text is reader-visible in the current CarePlan boundaries and relationships discussion. The change affects explanatory specification content by replacing misleading status-of-planned wording with current request intent language and by restoring the outside-initiation-or-authorization nuance; it does not alter conformance resources or generated collateral.
triage.recommended_reviewer_action: Do not apply solely as an already-authorized Jira carry-forward. jira_evidence.explanation: This Published/Persuasive with Modification issue resolved to replace the DiagnosticRequest/CarePlan wording with text about CarePlan typically referencing DiagnosticRequest at plan or proposal stage, with requests sometimes requiring initiation and authorization outside the CarePlan. It strongly supports the substance of the proposed clarification, but by itself does not settle whether the current PC-owned CarePlan narrative should be changed without a new/current WG decision.

This Published/Persuasive issue combined DiagnosticRequest and ProcedureRequest, explaining why the original edited DiagnosticRequest page is no longer the current location for the old wording. It supports the historical refactoring path but does not itself require this CarePlan narrative update.
This later request-resource boundary and merge discussion helps explain the move toward the current ServiceRequest surface, but it does not directly authorize the CarePlan text change.

Known reviewer feedback says to defer for WG vote because the original decision was voted by OO, not Patient Care.

commits.subject: FHIR-27789: Require absolute canonical URL regex
commits.summary: Completed the published FHIR-27789 decision by tightening canonical resource URL invariants so canonical URLs must include an absolute URI scheme colon.

triage.reviewer_summary: This is a Jira-backed missed application: FHIR-27789 explicitly required CanonicalResource.url to be an absolute URI and to have a computable regex requiring a colon. The existing cnl-1 invariant still permitted relative canonical URLs, so tightening the invariant in the authoritative StructureDefinition sources completes the published decision.
triage.category_rationale: FHIR-27789 resolved that CanonicalResource.url SHALL be an absolute URI and that the regex include a ':' requirement in addition to the no-spaces URI baseline. The current source only partially applied that decision: the prose said absolute URI, but CanonicalResource.url and the active URL elements carrying cnl-1 still used expressions such as ^[^|# ]+$, which reject pipes, hashes, and spaces but accept relative strings without a URI scheme. These StructureDefinition XML files are authoritative conformance inputs, so the stale invariant affects rendered constraint text and validation/QA behavior for canonical-resource URL elements. Updating the human text and FHIRPath regex on CanonicalResource.url and the copied/inherited active URL constraints is required to make the computable rule match the Jira decision, not merely adjacent cleanup.
triage.fhir_spec_impact: The changed files are editor-owned StructureDefinition XML conformance sources. Their short descriptions and cnl-1 constraints feed current rendered element pages, generated conformance resources, and validation warning behavior for canonical resource URLs; before this change, the computable constraint contradicted the absolute-URI requirement by permitting relative values.
triage.recommended_reviewer_action: Keep the commit as the Jira-backed fix, subject to normal editorial review of the exact regex and confirmation that the affected elements are the active URL elements carrying the canonical URL constraint.

jira_evidence.explanation: The published persuasive resolution specifically says CanonicalResource.url SHALL be an absolute URI and that the regex should require ':' in addition to the no-spaces URI baseline. That directly requires a computable colon/scheme check on the canonical URL invariant.

This later issue introduced the cnl-1 invariant on CanonicalResource.url and ensured it manifested on resources inheriting URL to exclude '|' and '#'. It explains why the current invariant is present across these StructureDefinitions, but it did not satisfy FHIR-27789's separate colon requirement.

caveats: No hard-avoid generated files or layout-only SVGs are included; the commit changes only StructureDefinition XML conformance sources.
The regex preserves urn:oid: and urn:uuid: forms because it requires a URI scheme followed by ':' rather than requiring http or https.

commits.author: Josh Mandel
commits.subject: FHIR-27113: Correct REST trailing slash example
commits.summary: Corrected the RESTful API trailing-slash paragraph so the non-trailing resource-type example is the valid form [base]/[type].

triage.reviewer_summary: Jira-backed missed application: FHIR-27113 required the RESTful HTTP page to say that resource-type endpoints with and without a trailing slash are equivalent when either form is supported. The previous source applied the rule but left the non-trailing example malformed as [base]/type], and this commit corrects the rendered normative example.
triage.category_rationale: FHIR-27113 was resolved Published/Persuasive with Modification with concrete REST wording: servers SHALL support both forms, with and without a trailing slash, if they support either; servers are discouraged from redirecting only to achieve a canonical query URL; and servers may choose their own convention for Bundle.link[self]. The application of that resolution added the paragraph to source/http.html, but the non-trailing resource-type URL example was malformed as [base]/type], so the active RESTful API page did not correctly show the approved equivalent form [base]/[type]. Because source/http.html is the current RESTful API specification page, the malformed example is reader-visible normative HTTP guidance. Correcting it to [base]/[type], with punctuation cleanup in the same sentence, is required to complete the approved Jira application rather than optional consistency work or a separate policy change.
triage.fhir_spec_impact: The change affects source/http.html, the rendered RESTful API specification page. It corrects a malformed example inside a SHALL paragraph; it does not change conformance resources or generated collateral, but it directly fixes current rendered normative guidance.
triage.recommended_reviewer_action: Keep this as a Jira-backed fix to the RESTful HTTP page. Review it as a narrow correction to the approved trailing-slash rule, not as a reopening of the redirect or canonicalization policy.

jira_evidence.explanation: The Jira was Published/Persuasive with Modification and specifically required RESTful HTTP language treating resource-type URLs with and without a trailing slash as equivalent forms when either is supported. The initial application added that paragraph but malformed the non-trailing example, so this correction is directly required by the resolved wording.

commits.author: Josh Mandel
commits.subject: FHIR-31491: Align named-query parameter scope notes
commits.summary: Aligned the OperationDefinition named-query notes with the FHIR-31491 Search-page rule for inherited search-parameter scope and support.

triage.reviewer_summary: This is a real fix needing attribution or FHIR-I confirmation: it removes a reader-visible inconsistency between the Search page and OperationDefinition named-query guidance. It should not be treated as a clean missed application of FHIR-31491 because the OperationDefinition paragraph being replaced was introduced by the later FHIR-39318 decision.
triage.category_rationale: FHIR-31491 clearly resolved the named-query rule for the Search page: standard all-resource and search-result parameters are potentially available, resource-specific parameters are potentially available when the query operation has a resource scope, inherited parameters need not be supported unless documented, and clients should rely on CapabilityStatement support for general searches. The current OperationDefinition notes are an active narrative surface and the pre-change text conflicts with those Search-page semantics by keeping older automatic-scope wording, tying resource-specific parameters to resources returned by the operation, and requiring supported parameters to be listed in OperationDefinition. However, the evidence does not prove a clean Jira-backed missed application for this whole commit: FHIR-31491's concrete resolution targeted the Search-section sentence, while FHIR-39318 later specifically resolved OperationDefinition named-query wording that closely matches the paragraph now being changed. The edit is substantively appropriate as cross-page consistency work, but replacing a later work-group-resolved paragraph should have an explicit attribution or confirmation path.
triage.fhir_spec_impact: The changed file is OperationDefinition resource narrative, so the text is reader-visible on the current OperationDefinition page. The change affects implementer understanding of named-query inherited search-parameter scope and support; it does not alter conformance resource structure, validation behavior, examples, or generated-only collateral.
triage.recommended_reviewer_action: Consider the edit as a real OperationDefinition/Search consistency fix, but route it through FHIR-I confirmation or a follow-up issue that explicitly reconciles FHIR-31491 and FHIR-39318 rather than applying it solely as a missed FHIR-31491 application.

jira_evidence.explanation: The resolution directly defines the desired named-query semantics for standard, resource-scoped, and inherited search parameters, server support, CapabilityStatement assumptions, and optional documentation of supported parameters. It strongly supports the substance of the proposed wording, but its concrete source instruction was to replace text in the Search section, not to revise the later OperationDefinition notes paragraph.

This later named-query issue specifically requested OperationDefinition-page narrative and its resolution text closely matches the paragraph being changed, including common/resource-returned parameters and explicit OperationDefinition listing. That makes it the more relevant attribution for the current OperationDefinition surface, but it does not by itself justify replacing that wording with the FHIR-31491/Search-page formulation.

The named-query examples discussion supports treating resource-scoped parameters such as Patient.birthdate as usable in Patient-scoped named queries when supported, but it does not require this specific OperationDefinition notes edit.

caveats: There are no generated, derived, SVG, or editor-avoided files in this commit; the concern is attribution and decision authority, not file scope.

The Search page already contains the FHIR-31491 wording, while the OperationDefinition notes paragraph reflects later FHIR-39318-style wording, so reviewers should decide whether the later paragraph was an intentional narrowing or an inconsistency to correct.

triage.fhir_spec_impact: source/terminologies.html is reader-visible terminology guidance. The stale wording could lead implementers or validators to treat translation Codings or CodeableConcept text as prohibited by a maximum binding, instead of requiring that at least one Coding satisfy the maximum value set while permitting other representations of the same concept.
triage.recommended_reviewer_action: Keep this as the Jira-backed terminology clarification. No generated or editor-avoided files are involved.

jira_evidence.explanation: The issue reported published examples whose system values used ValueSet URLs instead of the code systems used by those ValueSets and gave the correct source/spec behavior: examples must use the CodeSystem URL in system positions. The current changed files repeat that invalid pattern in active example/terminology surfaces, so this is the direct Jira basis.

The implemented terminology proposal created the THO Time Period Ranges CodeSystem and ValueSet, with the final code system at http://terminology.hl7.org/CodeSystem/time-period-ranges. It supports the exact replacement URI for the Measure age-range ValueSet and HIV Indicators CQL, but the need to stop using a ValueSet URI as a code system comes from FHIR-8712.

This Measure terminology issue provides related background for Measure stratifier terminology and mentions the newer terminology work, but its resolution is about renaming/alignment of the Measure Stratifier Type example and does not itself require this ValueSet-as-system cleanup.

This later Group terminology migration decision says the Group value sets and underlying code systems should move to THO while keeping the existing Group Code URL. It does not conflict with using http://hl7.org/fhir/group-code as the current CodeSystem URI in the examples.

triage.tooling_recommendation: Add or strengthen a publisher/QA check that flags ValueSet canonicals used in Coding.system, ValueSet.compose.include.system, and CQL codesystem declarations so invalid examples are not silently published.
caveats: The original FHIR-8712 example was an older ImmunizationRecommendation case that is no longer present; these files are later regressions of the same concrete invalid system-URL pattern.
The remaining disabled legacy source/us ValueSet-as-system pattern should not be folded into this change unless that source is reactivated and shown to affect current output.

commits.author: Josh Mandel
commits.subject: FHIR-7795: Correct IG global profile reference
commits.summary: Corrected the active CapabilityStatement.implementationGuide comment so it points to ImplementationGuide.global, the current default-profile mechanism that resolved the original fan-out reference-profiling problem.

triage.reviewer_summary: Jira-backed missed application, but the closest attribution is the later CapabilityStatement clarification rather than only the older default-profile issue. The edit fixes an active conformance comment that pointed readers and generated StructureDefinition metadata at non-existent Implementation.global definitions instead of ImplementationGuide.global.
triage.category_rationale: FHIR-39433 specifically resolved to add clarifying notes to CapabilityStatement.implementationGuide explaining that asserting an IG means adhering to the IG's global definitions and general textual requirements, while CapabilityStatement.instantiates is used for conformance to CapabilityStatements in the IG. That resolution was applied with the element name Implementation.global, but the current active IG-wide default-profile element is ImplementationGuide.global, so the application left the CapabilityStatement.implementationGuide comment referring to a non-existent element. Because this comment is part of the authoritative CapabilityStatement StructureDefinition, it affects rendered element documentation and generated conformance metadata. Replacing Implementation.global with ImplementationGuide.global is required to make the applied clarification identify the actual current element rather than being adjacent cleanup.
triage.fhir_spec_impact: The changed file is an authoritative StructureDefinition for CapabilityStatement, and the edited comment is surfaced as element documentation/conformance metadata for CapabilityStatement.implementationGuide. The stale wording was misleading in current output because there is no Implementation.global element, while ImplementationGuide.global is the active mechanism for IG-wide global/default profile assertions.
triage.recommended_reviewer_action: Keep the source fix as a Jira-backed correction, but treat FHIR-39433 as the direct clarification that was misapplied and FHIR-7795 as supporting history for the ImplementationGuide.global mechanism.

jira_evidence.explanation: This later published clarification explicitly required notes on CapabilityStatement.implementationGuide about the meaning of asserting an implementation guide versus instantiating its CapabilityStatements. The applied text named Implementation.global, but the intended/current IG-wide element is ImplementationGuide.global, making this the direct missed application.

This persuasive issue established the ImplementationGuide/default-profile solution for avoiding fan-out profiling of references. It supports why ImplementationGuide.global is the right target, but it did not by itself require the later CapabilityStatement.implementationGuide wording.

This companion profiling issue is part of the same default-profile problem space and refers back to the FHIR-7795 approach, but it does not independently require this CapabilityStatement comment correction.

caveats: The commit changes only source/capabilitystatement/structuredefinition-CapabilityStatement.xml; no generated, derived, SVG, or out-of-build files are included.
FHIR-7795 is useful historical support, but reviewers should cite FHIR-39433 for the concrete CapabilityStatement.implementationGuide clarification.
